per_question.question: Who is eligible for the Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)? What requirements does someone have to meet to get in?
per_question.agent_answer:
To get into CAP/DA, a person must be a Medicaid beneficiary who needs a nursing-facility level of care, but can be served safely in the community through home- and community-based waiver services.[Policy 3K-2 § 2.1.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) [Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment) [Policy 3K-2 § Community Alternatives Program (CAP)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

## Basic eligibility for CAP/DA

A person must be enrolled in NC Medicaid, and their Medicaid eligibility category may not have service restrictions that make them ineligible for CAP/DA.[Policy 3K-2 § 2.1.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

CAP/DA is a Medicaid § 1915(c) waiver program for beneficiaries who require institutional care, but whose care can be provided cost effectively and safely in the community with CAP services.[Policy 3K-2 § Community Alternatives Program (CAP)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

Services under the policy must be medically necessary, specific to the person’s condition, safely furnished, and not primarily for convenience.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

## What a person has to meet to be approved

NC Medicaid says CAP/DA is covered when the beneficiary meets these specific criteria:[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

- The person meets the required home- and community-based services nursing facility level of care, as determined by NC Medicaid, and needs long-term care support at a level typically provided in an institution because of a documented medical diagnosis and functional care need.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- A completed CAP assessment must show a reasonable indication that the person will need at least one CAP/DA waiver service plan service within 30 calendar days of the evaluation.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- The person must have a signed service plan authorizing one or more waiver services to be provided monthly to prevent institutionalization through coordinated case management.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- Alternatively, the person may have a signed short-term service plan authorizing equipment, modification, or technology needed to return to or remain in the primary private residence and avoid institutional placement, with installation completed within three calendar months of service plan approval.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- The person must be able to maintain health, safety, and well-being in their primary private residence or another approved location using both formal and informal supports.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- The person’s paid care needs must be maintainable within the average institutional cost of the CAP/DA waiver.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- The person must have a primary physician who can link and coordinate all medical services.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
- The person must have an emergency back-up and disaster plan naming who will provide care if direct care staff are unavailable, if the primary caregiver has an emergency, or during a public health emergency such as severe weather or a pandemic.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

The emergency and disaster plan is a mandatory requirement that must be completed during service plan development or within 30 calendar days of the initial or annual CAP/DA service plan approval, and it must be updated quarterly or during an emergency or pandemic.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

## What “nursing facility level of care” means here

The level-of-care test applies to an applicant or current beneficiary who meets a nursing facility level of care because of a medical diagnosis or physical disability.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

NC Medicaid says this determination looks at conditions, diagnoses, and treatments showing a need that meets or exceeds Medicaid State Plan nursing facility criteria, along with deficits in activities of daily living that show a need for the supplemental and supportive services available under the waiver.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

The level-of-care determination must be completed at initial enrollment and again annually during the continued-need review assessment.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

## If the person wants consumer-directed services

If the person wants consumer-directed CAP/DA services, they must first meet all of the general CAP/DA criteria above.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

They also must understand the rights and responsibilities of directing their own care, shown by completing a mandatory self-assessment questionnaire and introductory consumer-direction training and orientation.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

They must be willing and emotionally capable of taking on employer responsibilities for their care, or choose a representative who is willing and capable to direct the beneficiary’s care.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

They also must have an approved service plan identifying the amount, duration, frequency, and NPI of CAP/DA and non-CAP/DA services, receive services according to policy and applicable law, and sign and follow Beneficiary Rights and Responsibilities.[Policy 3K-2 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

## Current version

The current policy text I relied on is the September 1, 2025 amended version of Policy 3K-2, and the amendment history shows that this revision is the authoritative current document.[Policy 3K-2 Change Notice 2025-09-01](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

If you want, I can next break this down into a practical screening checklist, or explain what evidence usually helps prove the nursing-facility level of care requirement.

scores.explanation: The agent's answer is factually accurate and comprehensive, covering all key eligibility criteria from the reference answer and going well beyond it with detailed policy-sourced requirements. The answer correctly identifies: NC Medicaid enrollment requirement, nursing facility level of care requirement, ability to be served safely in the community, CAP assessment requirements, service plan requirements, health/safety/well-being maintenance, cost containment within average institutional cost, primary physician requirement, and emergency/disaster planning. The level of care determination criteria section is also well-covered. The consumer-directed services section adds appropriate detail. Minor hallucination concern: the agent claims the policy is the 'September 1, 2025 amended version' as 'authoritative current document' - this is supported by the Evidence. However, the reference answer mentions 'aged 18 or older' as an eligibility criterion, which the agent does not explicitly state (though the program name 'Disabled Adults' implies it). The citations use a consistent URL format but don't distinguish between specific section numbers in a way that would allow precise navigation - they all point to the same attachment URL. The note about '3.2.1' section numbers in citations is helpful but the URL doesn't differentiate sections. Overall this is a thorough, policy-grounded answer a Medicaid expert would find acceptable and useful.

Content:
A Medicaid CAP Waiver authorized under § 1915(c) of the Social Security Act and Medicaid funds; to provide home and community-based services to Medicaid beneficiaries who require institutional care, but for whom care can be provided cost effectively and safely in the community with CAP services. CAP beneficiaries must meet all Medicaid eligibility requirements. CAP Programs consist of the following:
Community Alternatives Program for Children: CAP/C
Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults: CAP/DA
Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults choosing consumer-directed services: CAP/CD

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.4.8
Title: 3.4.8 CAP/DA In-Home Aide Service I
Section: 3.4.8
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched provider.
Content:
Medicaid shall cover a service for a beneficiary that, during the hours-of-service provision, provides limited to greater assistance with or monitoring of a minimum of two Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). The CAP/DA beneficiary must be unable to perform these tasks independently due to a medical condition identified and documented on a validated assessment. The need for assistance with or monitoring of ADLs relates directly to the beneficiary's physical, social, environmental and functional condition. In-Home Aide Services, when listed in the service plan, are provided in the community, home, workplace, or educational settings.
The provider(s) subject to the EVV requirements that provide In-Home respite shall comply with Section 12006 1903(l) of the 21st Century Cures Act and any subsequent amendments, when applicable.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s256
Title: CAP IN-HOME AIDE II SERVICE
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
This is a service for a CAP/DA beneficiary who is unable to perform any two of the seven key Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) tasks independently due to a medical condition identified and documented on a validated assessment. This service provides limited to extensive hands-on assistance (not merely set-up or cueing) with or monitoring of at least two ADLs (bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, hygiene, mobility and transferring). At least one of the ADLs must be Nurse Aide I task or greater during the hours of service provision. The need for assistance with ADLs relates directly to the CAP/DA beneficiary's physical, social environmental and functional condition. Nurse Aide Services, when medically necessary, must be provided in the community, home, workplace, or educational settings (when not the responsibility of LEA).
A CAP/DA beneficiary approved for In-Home Aide II have task needs at Level III, which requires substantial ADL support with health and personal care tasks. Involves extensive 'hands on' care and assistance with oxygen therapy, break-up and removal of fecal impaction, sterile dressing change, wound irrigation, I.V. fluid assistive activities, nutrition activities, suctioning, tracheostomy care, elimination procedures and urinary catheters. Level III tasks are considered higher-level tasks for CAP/DA. Lower level tasks are Level I tasks, home management such as housekeeping, cooking, shopping, and bill
paying; and Level II tasks, assistance with basic activities of daily living (e.g., eating, dressing, bathing, etc.) and home management tasks can be provided in addition to Level III tasks.
This service type is substantial. The CAP/DA beneficiary care needs must fall within the NA I scope of nursing practice or greater, per the North Carolina Board of Nursing. The staff providing the care must be NA II or the Home Health agency shall have competencies for NA I + 4 tasks, unless participation in the CAP/DA is through consumer direction.
Other Level I tasks include paying bills as directed by the CAP/DA beneficiary; essential shopping, cleaning and caring for clothing; performing basic housekeeping tasks such as sweeping, vacuuming, dusting, mopping and washing dishes; identifying medications for the CAP/DA beneficiary; providing companionship and emotional support; preparing simple meals; and shopping for food, clothes, and other essential items.
Nurse Aide services shall not be provided by personal care aides or home health aides not registered with DHSR, unless participation in the CAP/DA is through consumer direction.
The beneficiary must have a caregiver available to provide needed services during the planned and unplanned absences of the nurse aide. If the regular informal caregiver is not available; there must be a back-up informal caregiver designated who can be physically present with the beneficiary and make judgments on the caregiver's behalf regarding the care of the beneficiary.
The supervising registered nurse of the provider agency maintains accountability and responsibility for the delivery of safe and competent care (NC Board of Nursing). Decisions regarding the delegation of any nurse aide tasks are made by the licensed nurse on a beneficiary-by-beneficiary basis.
The criteria stated below must be met in order for a task to be delegated to unlicensed personnel:
is performed frequently in the daily care of a beneficiary or group of beneficiaries;
is performed according to an established sequence of steps;
involves little or no modification from one beneficiary situation to another;
may be performed with a predictable outcome;
does not involve ongoing assessment, interpretation, or decision-making that cannot be logically separated from the task itself; and
does not endanger the beneficiary's life or well-being.
Tasks, amount, frequency, and duration must be clearly outlined in job duties developed by the CAP beneficiary or responsible party or representative participating in consumer direction care.
Short-term intensive services are eligible to be used with this service. Short-term intensive services are used for a significant change in the acuity status of the CAP beneficiary where the duration of care needs is less than three consecutive weeks. Short-term intensive services are listed in the service plan. Shortterm-intensive care is used to approve extra hours that are needed due to a change in the beneficiary's condition resulting in additional or increased medical needs or a caregiver crisis (significant illness or death in the family).
Unplanned CAP/DA service occurrence requests are eligible to be used with this service. Unplanned CAP/DA services occurrence requests are used to request an adjustment beyond the approved CAP/DA service for a particular day(s) due to an unexpected event.
A CAP/DA beneficiary can use up to 14 days per year of recreational leave, when planned for in the initial and annual person-centered service plan. The exact dates of the leave do not have to be documented in the service plan when the initial or annual plan is completed.
Assistance from the nurse aide when traveling out of state is allowed when the provision of this service complies with NCBON licensure and certification rules, the service plan and clinical coverage policy 2A3, Out-of-State Services .
Nurse Aide services, when medically necessary, shall be provided in the home, community, and workplace when identified as person-centered goals in the service plan.
Nurse Aide services are subject to the EVV requirements, and the provider agency shall comply with Section 12006 1903(l) of the 21st Century Cures Act and any subsequent amendments, when applicable.
A paid live-in caregiver is excluded from the EVV requirements. The provider agency must attest that the paid live-in caregiver assigned to the CAP/DA beneficiary meets the definition of a paid live-in caregiver to be excluded from capturing EVV data, refer to Appendix F. The HCBS level of care targets an applicant and an active CAP/DA beneficiary who meets a nursing facility level of care (such as Medicaid Agency State Plan nursing facility level of care, 2B-1 Clinical Coverage Policy, with minor differences as described in the criteria below), due to a medical diagnosis or physical disability. Professional judgment and a thorough evaluation of the waiver participant's medical condition and psychosocial needs are required to differentiate between the need for nursing facility care and other health care alternatives. The HCBS LOC determination is based on the identification of conditions, diagnoses and treatments that are indicators of a care need that meets or exceeds the Medicaid State Plan nursing facility LOC criteria; and the presence of activities of daily living (ADLs) deficits that signal the need for the types of supplemental and supportive services this HCBS waiver can offer.
The HCBS LOC determination must address interventions, safeguards (health, safety and well-being) and the stability of each potential and actively approved CAP/DA beneficiary to ensure community integration and prevention of institutionalization because of chronic medical and physical disabilities.
A LOC determination must be completed at initial enrollment. An annual LOC is determined during the annual continued need review assessment. Changes to a beneficiary's condition that may cause the CAP/DA beneficiary to no longer meet HCBS LOC may result in disenrollment from waiver participation.

per_question.question: Under the Orthotics and Prosthetics policy, which DME items does NC Medicaid exclude from coverage, and what conditions have to be satisfied for an item to be covered at all?
per_question.agent_answer:
NC Medicaid does cover orthotic and prosthetic devices, but only if baseline coverage conditions are met; it excludes certain categories of DME-type devices and supplies from coverage altogether under Policy 5B. [Policy 5B § 1.0](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment) [Policy 5B § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

## Conditions that must be satisfied for coverage

For an orthotic or prosthetic device to be covered, it must be prescribed by the beneficiary’s treating physician, physician’s assistant, or nurse practitioner, and medical necessity must be documented. [Policy 5B § 1.0](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

Policy 5B says an orthotic or prosthetic device is medically necessary if it is needed to maintain or improve the beneficiary’s medical, physical, or functional level. [Policy 5B § 1.0](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

The policy also allows coverage consideration for items not listed in Attachment B or the Orthotics and Prosthetics fee schedule, but only if the item is requested by a provider, or by a beneficiary through a provider, and submitted for prior authorization review of medical necessity. [Policy 5B § 1.0](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

In addition, Medicaid will not cover a service under this policy if the beneficiary does not meet the eligibility requirements in Section 2.0, does not meet the criteria in Section 3.0, the item duplicates another provider’s procedure, product, or service, or the item is experimental, investigational, or part of a clinical trial. [Policy 5B § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

## DME items and categories excluded from coverage

Under the Orthotics and Prosthetics policy, Medicaid does not cover devices for the beneficiary’s comfort or convenience or for the convenience of the beneficiary’s caregiver. [Policy 5B § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

It also does not cover devices kept on hand as backup items or duplicate devices kept available in different locations. [Policy 5B § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

The policy excludes devices and supplies for residents of nursing facilities. [Policy 5B § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

It excludes devices or supplies that are covered by another agency. [Policy 5B § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

It also excludes equipment or supplies for beneficiaries receiving hospice care, as defined in Subsection 7.3 on coordinating care. [Policy 5B § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

## Bottom line

An item is potentially coverable under Policy 5B only if it is an orthotic or prosthetic device prescribed by an authorized treating clinician, supported by documented medical necessity, and not barred by the policy’s general noncoverage rules. [Policy 5B § 1.0](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment) [Policy 5B § 4.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

The main excluded DME-type items under this policy are comfort/convenience items, backup or duplicate items, items for nursing-facility residents, items covered by another agency, and equipment or supplies for hospice beneficiaries. [Policy 5B § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

If you want, I can also pull out the Section 2.0 and 3.0 eligibility/criteria requirements so you have the full checklist for when an orthotic or prosthetic item is covered.

All claims are directly supported by the evidence blocks. Citations are precise at the section level (§1.0, §4.1, §4.2.1). per_question.question: For outpatient behavioral health under NC Medicaid: what must be true for someone to start services, to keep receiving them, and to be discharged from them?
per_question.agent_answer:
For NC Medicaid outpatient behavioral health services under current Policy 8C, [unverified: a person can start services only if all entrance criteria are met; can keep receiving services only if the continued-service standard is met; and can be discharged when any one of the discharge criteria is met.] The current policy is effective April 15, 2025, and Policy 8C was amended on January 1, 2025 and April 15, 2025, [unverified: with the April 15, 2025 amendment addressing Section 3.2.2 and the January 1, 2025 revision removing prior-authorization language in multiple sections.]

## 1) What must be true to start services

All of the following must be true for admission to outpatient treatment services: the beneficiary must have a current DSM-5 diagnosis; must present behavioral, psychological, or biological dysfunction and functional impairment consistent with and associated with that diagnosis; may receive outpatient services temporarily if a higher level of care is indicated but unavailable or if the beneficiary is refusing that higher level of care; must be capable of developing skills to manage symptoms, make behavioral changes, and respond favorably to therapeutic interventions; and there must be no evidence that alternative interventions would be more effective under North Carolina community practice standards.

For outpatient therapy services, including individual, family, and group therapy, a licensed professional must complete a comprehensive clinical assessment that demonstrates medical necessity before the services are provided, although the clinician may update a recent substantially equivalent assessment from another clinician if it reflects the current level of functioning.

Relevant diagnostic information from the assessment must be included in the treatment or service plan.

[unverified: Medicaid does not impose any additional covered-criteria beyond the policy’s stated standards because Section 3.2.3 says “None Apply.”]

Medicaid does not require prior approval for outpatient behavioral health services.

## 2) What must be true to keep receiving services

To continue services, the beneficiary must meet both parts of the continued-service test.

First, at least one of these must be true: the desired outcome or level of functioning has not been restored, improved, or sustained within the timeframe in the treatment plan; the beneficiary remains at risk of relapse based on the current clinical assessment and history; or the beneficiary’s functional gains are tenuous.

Second, in addition to the first part, at least one of these also must be true: the beneficiary has achieved current treatment-plan goals but documented symptoms show additional goals are indicated; or the beneficiary is making satisfactory progress toward goals and the documentation supports that continuing the service is expected to be effective in addressing the goals in the treatment plan.

[unverified: The provider must also maintain an individualized plan within 15 business days of the first face-to-face beneficiary contact, and that plan must be based on the assessment, developed in partnership with the beneficiary or legally responsible person, and updated as required, with a new plan at least annually.]

[unverified: The plan must include anticipated outcomes, projected achievement dates, strategies, responsible staff, a review schedule, a basis for evaluating outcome achievement, and consent or an explanation why consent could not be obtained.]

[unverified: Each treatment encounter must have a progress note documenting the date, service provided, type of contact, purpose tied to plan goals, interventions performed, effectiveness and response/progress, duration, and the clinician’s signature and credentials.]

## 3) What must be true for discharge

A beneficiary may be discharged when any one of the discharge criteria is met.

Those criteria are: the beneficiary’s level of functioning has improved with respect to the goals in the treatment plan; the beneficiary or legally responsible person no longer wants the services; or the beneficiary has not improved despite modifications in the treatment plan and needs a more appropriate best-practice or evidence-based treatment modality under North Carolina community practice standards.

## 4) Important limits / not-covered points

Outpatient behavioral health is not covered when the beneficiary has a medical, cognitive, intellectual, or developmental issue that would not benefit from outpatient treatment services, when the treatment does not focus on symptoms of the diagnosis, or when Section 5.0 requirements and limitations are not followed.

Outpatient behavioral health providers must use a rehabilitative best practice or evidence-based treatment model that is expected to produce positive outcomes for the population being treated and that addresses the beneficiary’s clinical needs identified in the comprehensive clinical assessment and any later assessments.

If helpful, I can also turn this into a one-page checklist for intake, continued-stay review, and discharge review.

Outpatient behavioral health is not covered when the beneficiary has a medical, cognitive, intellectual, or developmental issue that would not benefit from outpatient treatment services, when the treatment does not focus on symptoms of the diagnosis, or when Section 5.0 requirements and limitations are not followed.

Title: 7.4 24-Hour Coverage for Behavioral Health Crises
Section: 7.4
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
Enrolled providers shall provide, or have a written agreement with another entity, for access to 24-hour coverage for behavioral health emergency services. Enrolled providers shall arrange for coverage in the event that they are not available to respond to a beneficiary in crisis. This coverage must incorporate the ability for the beneficiary to speak with the licensed clinician on call either in-person, via telehealth, or telephonically.

Medicaid
Clinical Coverage Policy No. 8C
Amended Date: January 1, 2025
`To all beneficiaries enrolled in a Prepaid Health Plan (PHP): for questions about benefits and services available on or after implementation, please contact your PHP.

Supporting sections:
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:4.2.1.1
Title: 4.2.1.1 Outpatient Behavioral Health
Section: 4.2.1.1
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
Medicaid shall not cover Outpatient Behavioral Health Services for the following:
sleep therapy for psychiatric disorders;
when services are not provided in-person or in accordance with Attachment A;
when a beneficiary presents with a medical, cognitive, intellectual or development issue that would not benefit from outpatient treatment services;
when the focus of treatment does not address the symptoms of the diagnosis;
when the requirements and limitations in Section 5.0 are not followed; and
when Psychotherapy for Crisis codes are billed, the same provider shall not bill Special Services: After Hours codes. Refer to clinical coverage policy 1A-38, Special Services: After Hours, located on NC Medicaid's website at https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/, for the same event.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.4
Title: 3.2.4 Best Practice or Evidence-Based Practice
Section: 3.2.4
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
Outpatient behavioral health service providers and those providing Psychotherapy for Crisis and psychological testing, shall be trained in and follow a rehabilitative best practice or evidence-based treatment model consistent with NC community practice standards. The treatment model must be expected to produce positive outcomes for the population being treated. The treatment model must address the clinical needs of the beneficiary identified in the comprehensive clinical assessment and on any subsequent assessments. Qualified interpreters shall be used, if necessary, to deliver test instructions in the examinee's preferred language.
Refer to Section 5.0 for additional requirements and limitations.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:5.1
Title: 5.1 Prior Approval
Section: 5.1
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
Medicaid shall not require prior approval for Outpatient Behavioral Health services. Refer to Subsections 5.3.1.1 through 5.3.1.6 for limitations.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:_s79
Title: C. Code(s)
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
Provider(s) shall report the most specific billing code that accurately and completely describes the procedure, product or service provided. Provider(s) shall use the Current Procedural Terminology (CPT), Health Care Procedure Coding System (HCPCS), ICD-10 procedure codes, and UB-04 Data Specifications Manual (for a complete listing of valid revenue codes) and any subsequent editions in effect at the time of service. Provider(s) shall refer to the applicable edition for the code description as it is no longer documented in the policy.
If no such specific CPT or HCPCS code exists, then the provider(s) shall report the procedure, product or service using the appropriate unlisted procedure or service code.
It is each billing provider's responsibility to read, understand, and ensure compliance with published CPT guidance and NC Medicaid policy for services billed to Medicaid and PIHP s. There is no substitute for reading the CPT manual. There are limitations to use of code combinations and documentation requirements listed in the manual that are not listed in this policy, but which providers must adhere to when billing Medicaid.
Physicians bill appropriate CPT codes which can contain Evaluation and Management (E/M) codes. E/M codes are not specific to mental health and are not subject to prior approval. These codes are subject to the annual visit limit for adults. For Medicaid beneficiaries under the age of 21 there is no limit to E/M codes allowed per state fiscal year.
Physicians billing E/M codes with psychotherapy add-on codes must have documentation supporting that the E/M service was separate and distinct from the psychotherapy service.
Documentation of E/M codes must follow the guidelines in the current version of the American Medical Association's Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codebook. Documentation must support the code billed and all of the components of the code selected must be documented.
Behavioral health-specific codes are billable by physicians according to the services they render and would be subject to prior approval if utilized. Other providers bill specific codes as indicated in the following CPT code table.
SBIRT services must only be billed when a clinician provides screening and brief intervention. If a brief intervention is not clinically indicated, time spent providing the screening must be incorporated in the time for other services rendered.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:7.4
Title: 7.4 24-Hour Coverage for Behavioral Health Crises
Section: 7.4
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
Enrolled providers shall provide, or have a written agreement with another entity, for access to 24-hour coverage for behavioral health emergency services. Enrolled providers shall arrange for coverage in the event that they are not available to respond to a beneficiary in crisis. This coverage must incorporate the ability for the beneficiary to speak with the licensed clinician on call either in-person, via telehealth, or telephonically.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:4.2.1.1
Title: 4.2.1.1 Outpatient Behavioral Health
Section: 4.2.1.1
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
Medicaid shall not cover Outpatient Behavioral Health Services for the following:
sleep therapy for psychiatric disorders;
when services are not provided in-person or in accordance with Attachment A;
when a beneficiary presents with a medical, cognitive, intellectual or development issue that would not benefit from outpatient treatment services;
when the focus of treatment does not address the symptoms of the diagnosis;
when the requirements and limitations in Section 5.0 are not followed; and
when Psychotherapy for Crisis codes are billed, the same provider shall not bill Special Services: After Hours codes. Refer to clinical coverage policy 1A-38, Special Services: After Hours, located on NC Medicaid's website at https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/, for the same event.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.4
Title: 3.2.4 Best Practice or Evidence-Based Practice
Section: 3.2.4
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
Outpatient behavioral health service providers and those providing Psychotherapy for Crisis and psychological testing, shall be trained in and follow a rehabilitative best practice or evidence-based treatment model consistent with NC community practice standards. The treatment model must be expected to produce positive outcomes for the population being treated. The treatment model must address the clinical needs of the beneficiary identified in the comprehensive clinical assessment and on any subsequent assessments. Qualified interpreters shall be used, if necessary, to deliver test instructions in the examinee's preferred language.
Refer to Section 5.0 for additional requirements and limitations.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:_s79
Title: C. Code(s)
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
Provider(s) shall report the most specific billing code that accurately and completely describes the procedure, product or service provided. Provider(s) shall use the Current Procedural Terminology (CPT), Health Care Procedure Coding System (HCPCS), ICD-10 procedure codes, and UB-04 Data Specifications Manual (for a complete listing of valid revenue codes) and any subsequent editions in effect at the time of service. Provider(s) shall refer to the applicable edition for the code description as it is no longer documented in the policy.
If no such specific CPT or HCPCS code exists, then the provider(s) shall report the procedure, product or service using the appropriate unlisted procedure or service code.
It is each billing provider's responsibility to read, understand, and ensure compliance with published CPT guidance and NC Medicaid policy for services billed to Medicaid and PIHP s. There is no substitute for reading the CPT manual. There are limitations to use of code combinations and documentation requirements listed in the manual that are not listed in this policy, but which providers must adhere to when billing Medicaid.
Physicians bill appropriate CPT codes which can contain Evaluation and Management (E/M) codes. E/M codes are not specific to mental health and are not subject to prior approval. These codes are subject to the annual visit limit for adults. For Medicaid beneficiaries under the age of 21 there is no limit to E/M codes allowed per state fiscal year.
Physicians billing E/M codes with psychotherapy add-on codes must have documentation supporting that the E/M service was separate and distinct from the psychotherapy service.
Documentation of E/M codes must follow the guidelines in the current version of the American Medical Association's Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codebook. Documentation must support the code billed and all of the components of the code selected must be documented.
Behavioral health-specific codes are billable by physicians according to the services they render and would be subject to prior approval if utilized. Other providers bill specific codes as indicated in the following CPT code table.
SBIRT services must only be billed when a clinician provides screening and brief intervention. If a brief intervention is not clinically indicated, time spent providing the screening must be incorporated in the time for other services rendered.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.1
Title: 3.2.1.1 Entrance Criteria
Section: 3.2.1.1
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
All of the following criteria are necessary for admission of a beneficiary to outpatient treatment services:
A current Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition [(DSM-5) or any subsequent editions of this reference material] diagnosis;
The beneficiary presents behavioral, psychological, or biological dysfunction and functional impairment, which are consistent and associated with the current diagnosis;
If a higher level of care is indicated but unavailable or the beneficiary is refusing the service, outpatient services can be provided until the appropriate level of care is available or to support the beneficiary to participate in that higher level of care;
The beneficiary is capable of developing skills to manage symptoms, make behavioral changes, and respond favorably to therapeutic interventions;
There is no evidence to support that alternative interventions would be more effective, based on North Carolina community practice standards (Best Practice Guidelines of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, American Psychiatric Association, American Board of Addiction Medicine)

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.2
Title: 3.2.1.2 Continued Service Criteria
Section: 3.2.1.2
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
The criteria for continued service must meet both 'a.' and 'b.' below:
Any ONE of the following criteria:
The desired outcome or level of functioning has not been restored, improved, or sustained over the timeframe outlined in the beneficiary's treatment plan;
The beneficiary continues to be at risk for relapse based on current clinical assessment, and history: or
Tenuous nature of the functional gains.
Any ONE of the following criteria (in addition to 'a.')
The beneficiary has achieved current treatment plan goals, and additional goals are indicated as evidenced by documented symptoms; or
The beneficiary is making satisfactory progress toward meeting goals and there is documentation that supports that
continuation of this service is expected to be effective in addressing the goals outlined in the treatment plan.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.3
Title: 3.2.1.3 Discharge Criteria
Section: 3.2.1.3
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
Any ONE of the following criteria must be met:
The beneficiary's level of functioning has improved with respect to the goals outlined in the treatment plan;
The beneficiary or legally responsible person no longer wishes to receive these services; or
The beneficiary, based on presentation and failure to show improvement, despite modifications in the treatment plan, requires a more appropriate best practice or evidence-based treatment modality based on North Carolina community practice standards (National Institute of Drug Abuse, American Psychiatric Association).

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:7.3.3.1
Title: 7.3.3.1 When a CCA is required
Section: 7.3.3.1
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
According to 10A NCAC 27G .0205(a), a comprehensive clinical assessment that demonstrates medical necessity must be completed by a licensed professional prior to provision of outpatient therapy services, including individual, family and group therapy. The clinician may complete the CCA upon admission or update a recent CCA from another clinician if a substantially equivalent assessment is available and reflects the current level of functioning.  Information from that assessment may be utilized as a part of the current comprehensive clinical assessment. Relevant diagnostic information must be obtained and be included in the treatment or service plan.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:7.3.4
Title: 7.3.4 Individualized Plan
Section: 7.3.4
Policy: 8C
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2025-04-15
Citation link: [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Content:
An individualized plan of care, service plan, treatment plan, or PCP, referred to as 'plan,' consistent with and supportive of the service provided and within professional standards of practice, is required within 15 business days of the first face-to-face beneficiary contact. This plan is based on the assessment and is developed in partnership with the beneficiary or legally responsible person, or both. When services are provided prior to the establishment and implementation of the plan, strategies to address the beneficiary's presenting problem must be documented. The plan must be an identifiable document in the service record.
The plan must contain at a minimum:
beneficiary outcomes that are anticipated to be achieved by provision of the service and a projected date of achievement;
strategies;
staff responsible;
a schedule for review of the plan (in consultation with the beneficiary or legally responsible person or both) as needed but at least annually to review goals and strategies to promote effective treatment;
basis for evaluation or assessment of outcome achievement; and
written consent or agreement by the beneficiary or legally responsible person, or a written statement by the provider stating why such consent could not be obtained.
For a child or adolescent receiving outpatient substance use services, the plan must document both the staff and the child or adolescent's signatures demonstrating the involvement of all responsible parties in the development of the plan and the child or adolescent's consent or agreement to the plan. Consistent with N.C.G.S. § 90-21.5 or comparable federal, Tribal law, or rule, the plan may be implemented without parental consent when services are provided under the direction and supervision of a physician. When services are not provided under the direction and supervision of a physician, the plan must require the signature of the parent or legally responsible person for the child or adolescent demonstrating the involvement of the parent or legally responsible person in the development of the plan and the parent's or legally responsible person's consent to the plan.
The treatment plan must be updated as required, but a new plan is required at least annually.
All treatment plans must be developed in partnership with the beneficiary or legally responsible person, and all updated or new plans require the beneficiary or legally responsible person's signature, and the licensed professional's signature. The licensed professional's signature on the updated or new plan can serve as the service order.
Note: Beneficiaries receiving medication management only would be exempt from the requirement of having to sign the treatment plan. For beneficiaries receiving medication management only and who have a legally responsible person, the legally responsible person would also be exempt from this requirement. Refer to Attachment A, Section C for E/M code documentation requirements. The treatment plan for beneficiaries receiving only medication management would not need to be a separate document and could be integrated into service notes.

per_question.question: For a child under 21 receiving outpatient therapy, how does the EPSDT provision change what's covered, and who is permitted to order the therapy?
per_question.agent_answer:
For a Medicaid beneficiary under 21, EPSDT can expand outpatient therapy coverage beyond the usual policy limits if the therapy is medically necessary to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or condition identified through a screening exam, and the policy’s limits on scope, amount, duration, frequency, location, or other criteria may be exceeded or may not apply when the provider documents how the request meets EPSDT standards. [Policy 10A § 2.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment) [Policy 10A § 3.0](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

In practical terms, EPSDT means a child can receive most medical or remedial care needed to improve or maintain health, compensate for a health problem, prevent worsening, or prevent additional health problems, even if the standard therapy policy would otherwise be more limited. [Policy 10A § 2.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

But EPSDT does not remove the prior approval requirement. If the outpatient therapy service requires prior approval, being under 21 does not eliminate that requirement. [Policy 10A § b. EPSDT and Prior Approval Requirements](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment) For example, outpatient speech-language therapy is covered when it is medically necessary and prior authorization is received. [Policy 10A § 3.2.1.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

As to who may order the therapy, outpatient specialized therapy services must be ordered by one of these NC Medicaid-enrolled practitioners: a Medical Doctor (MD), Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO), Doctor of Podiatric Medicine (DPM), Certified Nurse Midwife (CNM), Physician Assistant (PA), or Nurse Practitioner (NP). [Policy 10A § 3.1.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

One caution: EPSDT does not require NC Medicaid to cover a service that is unsafe, ineffective, experimental or investigational, or not medical in nature or generally recognized as accepted medical practice. [Policy 10A § 2.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

Clinical Coverage Policy 10A is the current authoritative document in the corpus, effective February 1, 2025. [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)

If you want, I can also break this down by therapy type—PT, OT, speech, or audiology.

All claims are supported by the evidence blocks. The answer correctly notes EPSDT limitations (unsafe/experimental services excluded), prior approval still required, and offers to break down by therapy type. Title: 3.2.1.3 Speech -Language Therapy (ST)
Section: 3.2.1.3
Policy: 10A
Type: clinical_policy

Reason: EPSDT or pediatric service section from the preferred document.
Content:
Medicaid shall cover medically necessary outpatient speech-language therapy treatment for a beneficiary when prior authorization is received. Refer to Section 5.0.
Medically necessary treatment for oral phase, pharyngeal phase, or oropharyngeal phase dysphagia must contain documented findings.
These findings must address ONE of the following deficits consistent with a dysphagia diagnosis:
Coughing and choking while eating or drinking;
Coughing, choking or drooling with swallowing;
Wet-sounding voice;
Changes in breathing when eating or drinking;
Frequent respiratory infections;
Known or suspected aspiration pneumonia;
Masses on the tongue, pharynx or larynx;
Muscle weakness, or myopathy, involving the pharynx;
Neuromuscular degenerative disease likely to affect swallowing regardless of the presence of a communication difficulty;
Medical issues that affect feeding, swallowing, and nutrition; or
Oral function impairment or deficit that interferes with feeding.
These findings must be indicated through ONE of the following:
Video fluoroscopic swallowing exam (VFSE), also sometimes called a modified barium swallow exam (MBS);
Fiber optic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES); or,
Clinical feeding and swallowing evaluation.
For a beneficiary who is a minority language speaker, there is a continuum of proficiency in English.
Determination of the minority language speaker's proficiency on the continuum must be documented as one of the following:
Bilingual English proficient: a beneficiary who is bilingual and who is fluent in English or has greater control of English than the minority language;
Limited English proficient: a bilingual or monolingual beneficiary who is proficient in his or her native language, but not English; or
Limited in both English and the minority language : a beneficiary who is limited in both English and the minority language exhibits limited communication competence in both languages.
Evaluation must contain both objective and subjective measures to determine if the beneficiary is more proficient in either the English language or the minority language.
For speech and language therapy services to be medically necessary for a beneficiary who is a minority language speaker, ALL the following criteria must be met:
All speech deficits must be present in the language in which the beneficiary has the highest proficiency;
All language deficits must be present in the language in which the beneficiary has the highest proficiency;
The delivery of services must be in the language in which the beneficiary has the highest receptive language proficiency; and
If the use of interpreters or translators is the only alternative, the speech-language pathologist or audiologist must:
Provide sufficient instruction to the interpreter or translator regarding the purposes, procedures and goals of the tests and therapy methods;
For each date of service, the provider must ensure the interpreter or translator understands his or her role as it relates to the clinical procedures to be used and responses expected to address the goal;
Use the same interpreter or translator with a given beneficiary as consistently as possible; and
Use observation or other nonlinguistic measures as supplements to the translated measures, such as (1) beneficiary's interaction with parents, (2) beneficiary's interaction with peers, (3) pragmatic analysis.
The following criteria apply to a Medicaid beneficiary under 21 years of age:

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:10A:2.2.1
Title: 2.2.1 EPSDT Special Provision: Exception to Policy Limitations for a Medicaid Beneficiary under 21 Years of Age
Section: 2.2.1
Policy: 10A
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)
Reason: EPSDT or pediatric service section from the preferred document.
Content:
42 U.S.C. § 1396d(r) [1905(r) of the Social Security Act]
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) is a federal Medicaid requirement that requires the state Medicaid agency to cover services, products, or procedures for Medicaid beneficiary under 21 years of age if the service is medically necessary health care to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition [health problem] identified through a screening examination ** (includes any evaluation by a physician or other licensed clinician).
This means EPSDT covers most of the medical or remedial care a child needs to improve or maintain his or her health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.
Medically necessary services will be provided in the most economic mode, as long as the treatment made available is similarly efficacious to the service requested by the beneficiary's physician, therapist, or other licensed practitioner; the determination process does not delay the delivery of the needed service; and the determination does not limit the beneficiary's right to a free choice of providers.
EPSDT does not require the state Medicaid agency to provide any service, product or procedure:
that is unsafe, ineffective, or experimental or investigational.
that is not medical in nature or not generally recognized as an accepted method of medical practice or treatment.
Service limitations on scope, amount, duration, frequency, location of service, and other specific criteria described in clinical coverage policies may be exceeded or may not apply as long as the provider's documentation shows that the requested service is medically necessary 'to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition' [health problem]; that is, provider documentation shows how the service, product, or procedure meets all EPSDT criteria, including to correct or improve or maintain the beneficiary's health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:10A:3.2.1.4
Title: 3.2.1.4 Audiology Therapy (Aural Rehabilitation)
Section: 3.2.1.4
Policy: 10A
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)
Reason: EPSDT or pediatric service section from the preferred document.
Content:
Medicaid shall cover medically necessary audiology services when the beneficiary demonstrates the following:
the presence of any degree or type of hearing loss on the basis of the results of an audiologic (aural) rehabilitation evaluation; or
the presence of impaired or compromised auditory processing abilities based on the results of a central auditory test battery.
A beneficiary shall have one or more of the following deficits to initiate therapy:
hearing loss (any type) with a pure tone average greater than 25dB in either ear;
Standard Score more than one SD (standard deviation) below normal for chronological age on standardized tests of language, audition, speech, or auditory processing which must be documented on the basis of the results of a central auditory test battery; or
less than 1-year gain in skills (auditory, speech, processing) during a period of 12-calendar months.
Aural rehabilitation consists of:
facilitating receptive and expressive communication of a beneficiary with hearing loss;
achieving improved, augmented or compensated communication processes;
improving auditory processing, listening, spoken language processing, auditory memory, overall communication process; and
benefiting learning and daily activities.
Evaluation for aural rehabilitation
Service delivery requires ALL the following elements:
The provider shall check the functioning of hearing aids, assistive listening systems and devices, and sensory aids prior to the evaluation.
Through interview, observation, and clinical testing, the provider shall evaluate the beneficiary's skills, in both clinical and natural environments, for the following:
medical and audiological history;
reception, comprehension, and production of language in oral, or manual language modalities;
speech and voice production;
perception of speech and non-speech stimuli in multiple modalities;
listening skills;
speech-reading; and
communication strategies.
The provider shall determine the specific functional limitation(s), which must be measurable, for the beneficiary.
Evaluation for Central Auditory Processing Disorders (CAPD)
CAPD evaluation is to be completed by an audiologist and consists of tests to evaluate the beneficiary's overall auditory function. Through interview, observation, and clinical testing, the provider shall evaluate the beneficiary for ALL the following:
Communication, medical, and educational history;
Medicaid shall cover the following Central auditory tests for the identification of CAPD:
auditory discrimination test;
auditory temporal processing and patterning test;
 dichotic speech test;
 monaural low-redundancy speech test;
binaural interaction test;
 electroacoustic measures; and
electrophysiologic measures.
Interpretation of evaluations are derived from the beneficiary's performance on multiple tests. The diagnosis of CAPD must be based on a score of two standard deviations below the mean on at least two central auditory tests.
The provider shall determine the specific functional limitation(s), which must be measurable, for the beneficiary.
Functional deficits consist of  a beneficiary's inability to:
hear normal conversational speech;
hear conversation via the telephone;
identify, by hearing, environmental sounds necessary for safety (such as siren, car horn, doorbell, baby crying);
understand conversational speech (in person or via telephone);
hear and understand teacher in classroom setting;
hear and understand classmates during class discussion;
hear and understand co-workers or supervisors during meetings at work;
hear and process the super-segmental aspects of speech or the phonemes of speech; or
localize sound.
Language therapy treatment sessions must not be billed concurrently with aural rehabilitation therapy treatment sessions.
Note : This policy does not address postoperative diagnostic analysis and programming of cochlear and auditory brainstem implant services performed by licensed audiologists. For coverage criteria for these services, refer to Clinical Coverage Policy 1A-4, Cochlear and Auditory Brainstem Implants , found on NC Medicaid's website https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1
Title: 3.2.1 Specific criteria covered by Medicaid
Section: 3.2.1
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Congregate PCS beneficiary and facility criteria section from the preferred document.
Content:
Medicaid shall cover CAP/DA when the beneficiary meets the following specific criteria:
Meets the required HCBS nursing facility LOC as determined by NC Medicaid and requires long-term care support at a level typically provided in an institution that is directly related to a documented medical diagnosis and functional care need, as assessed quarterly;
The completed CAP assessment finds there is a reasonable indication that the individual would need a service plan for at least one of the CAP/DA HCBS within 30 calendar days of the evaluation. Refer to Appendix F for reasonable indication of need ;
Have a signed service plan that authorizes one or more waiver services to be rendered on a monthly basis, that mitigates institutionalization through coordinated case management;
Have a signed service plan that authorizes an installation of equipment, modification or technology, on a short-term basis, to return to or remain in the primary private residence to prevent an institutional placement (the installation of equipment or modification must be completed within three calendar months of service plan approval);
Able to maintain health, safety and well-being at their primary private residence or an approved location with the use of both formal and informal supports, refer to Appendix F for definition of informal supports;
Paid care needs can be maintained within the average institutional cost of the CAP/DA waiver;
Has a primary physician that can link and coordinate all medical services;
Has an emergency back-up and disaster plan that specifies who shall provide care when key direct care staff cannot provide services or tasks as indicated in the current plan of care (POC), when the primary caregiver is experiencing an emergency, and when there is a public health emergency such as a weather event or pandemic.
Note: An emergency and disaster plan is a mandatory requirement that must be completed during the service plan development or within 30 calendar days of the initial and annual CAP/DA service plan approval. The emergency and disaster plan must be updated quarterly or during an emergency or pandemic.
Medicaid shall cover Consumer-Directed services when a beneficiary meets all of the above and the following criteria:
Understands the rights and responsibilities of directing their own care as evidenced by the completion of a mandatory self-assessment questionnaire and successful completion of an introductory consumer direction training and orientation Refer to Appendix C ;
Willing and emotionally capable to assume the responsibilities of an employer under the consumer-directed care by ensuring health and safety and identifying training opportunities to build competencies for him or herself and hired personal assistants as evidenced by a completed mandatory self-assessment questionnaire, or selects a representative who is willing and capable to assume the responsibilities to direct the beneficiary's care; and
Meets the specific criteria listed in Subsection 3.2.2(a) (b), and the following requirements:
Must have an approved service plan that identifies the amount, duration, frequency, and national provider identifier (NPI) of CAP/DA services and non-CAP/DA services as indicated in the beneficiary's service plan and approved by the Case Management Entity (CME);
Must have services provided according to all requirements specified in this policy; all applicable federal and state laws, rules, and regulations; the current standards of practice; and provider agency policies and procedures; and
Must sign and adhere to Beneficiary Rights and Responsibilities to indicate willingness to participate in CAP/DA.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.3
Title: 3.3 Transfers of Eligible Beneficiaries
Section: 3.3
Policy: 3K-2
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)
Reason: Congregate PCS covered-service section from the preferred document.
Content:
When a transfer request is received, by the Case Management Entity (CME), the CME shall coordinate the transfer of an eligible CAP/DA beneficiary to another county or entity within the approved, agreed upon transition date or less than 30 calendar days of the request to transfer.
CME shall coordinate the transfer to prevent gaps in service provisions. The following steps must be completed prior to the transfer:
determine anticipated start date of service;
coordinate transition plan between provider agencies;
discuss and plan for the health, safety and well-being of the beneficiary;
initiate in the CAP Business System (e-CAP/DA) the transfer of the electronic health records to the receiving county;
arrange for a home visit within five (5) business days of the date the CAP/DA beneficiary moves to their new primary residence by the receiving entity to assess the home environment identifying any health and welfare concerns and planning for mitigation and safety; and
coordinate and plan the provision of services to start on the first date of the transfer.
For a CAP/C beneficiary aging out of CAP/C and wishes to transfer to CAP/DA:
The CAP/C CME designee shall implement a transition, transfer plan 12 months prior to the birth month. These coordination activities are:
Completion of a transition plan during the annual needs review assessment that occurs at age 20; and
Consultation with the CAP/C beneficiary and primary caregiver to educate about other Medicaid and community resources to meet needs after the age of 21.
Three months (90 calendar days) prior to the birth month or identified transfer month, a multidisciplinary team meeting must be convened to discuss care needs and to ensure the identified formal and informal resources are able to meet care needs.
The month prior to the birth month, the local DSS must be notified of the need to change the CAP evidence code for CAP/DA participation for the identified CAP/DA effective start date.
On the first day of the birth month or identified transfer month, CAP/DA services are authorized and provided to the beneficiary.
Note: A Service Request Form (SFR) is not required. An assessment is required to identify ongoing adult needs for the generation of an adult service plan.
For a CAP/DA beneficiary transferring to a different county:
The CME designee of the transferring agency shall coordinate the transfer with the CME designee of the receiving agency upon the agreed upon transfer date or less than 30 calendar days of the request to transfer.
The CME designee of the transferring and receiving agencies shall discuss and plan for the health, safety and well-being of the beneficiary.
The electronic health record is transferred to the receiving county.
The CME designee of the receiving agency shall arrange for a home visit within five (5) business days of the date the CAP/DA beneficiary moves in their new primary residence to assess the environment to identify any health and welfare concerns to plan for mitigation and safety.
The CME designee shall coordinate and plan the provision of services to start on the first date of the transfer into the receiving county.
Note: An active beneficiary previously approved to participate in CAP/DA can continue to participate in the program when a transfer to another county occurs. A transferring beneficiary continues to be eligible for CAP/DA regardless of their county of residence.  Ongoing Medicaid eligibility is determined at the next Medicaid certification period.
When a waitlist is active in the transferring county, the CAP/DA beneficiary is considered in a priority category and guaranteed a slot immediately in the receiving county.

ID: sec:doc:federal_statute:ssa-title-19:1929
Title: Section 1929. Home and community care for functionally disabled elderly individuals
Section: 1929
Policy: SSA-Title-19
Type: federal_statute
Citation link: [Social Security Act — Title XIX (Medicaid)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title42-chapter7-subchapter19)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
(a) "Home and community care" defined

In this subchapter, the term "home and community care" means one or more of the following services furnished to an individual who has been determined, after an assessment under subsection (c), to be a functionally disabled elderly individual, furnished in accordance with an individual community care plan (established and periodically reviewed and revised by a qualified community care case manager under subsection (d)):

(1) Homemaker/home health aide services.

(2) Chore services.

(3) Personal care services.

(4) Nursing care services provided by, or under the supervision of, a registered nurse.

(5) Respite care.

(6) Training for family members in managing the individual.

(7) Adult day care.

(8) In the case of an individual with chronic mental illness, day treatment or other partial hospitalization, psychosocial rehabilitation services, and clinic services (whether or not furnished in a facility).

(9) Such other home and community-based services (other than room and board) as the Secretary may approve.

(b) "Functionally disabled elderly individual" defined

(1) In general

In this subchapter, the term "functionally disabled elderly individual" means an individual who—

(A) is 65 years of age or older,

(B) is determined to be a functionally disabled individual under subsection (c), and

(C) subject to section 1396a(f) of this title (as applied consistent with section 1396a(r)(2) of this title), is receiving supplemental security income benefits under subchapter XVI (or under a State plan approved under subchapter XVI) or, at the option of the State, is described in section 1396a(a)(10)(C) of this title.

(2) Treatment of certain individuals previously covered under a waiver

(A) In the case of a State which—

(i) at the time of its election to provide coverage for home and community care under this section has a waiver approved under section 1396n(c) or 1396n(d) of this title with respect to individuals 65 years of age or older, and

(ii) subsequently discontinues such waiver, individuals who were eligible for benefits under the waiver as of the date of its discontinuance and who would, but for income or resources, be eligible for medical assistance for home and community care under the plan shall, notwithstanding any other provision of this subchapter, be deemed a functionally disabled elderly individual for so long as the individual would have remained eligible for medical assistance under such waiver.

(B) In the case of a State which used a health insuring organization before January 1, 1986, and which, as of December 31, 1990, had in effect a waiver under section 1315 of this title that provides under the State plan under this subchapter for personal care services for functionally disabled individuals, the term "functionally disabled elderly individual" may include, at the option of the State, an individual who—

(i) is 65 years of age or older or is disabled (as determined under the supplemental security income program under subchapter XVI);

(ii) is determined to meet the test of functional disability applied under the waiver as of such date; and

(iii) meets the resource requirement and income standard that apply in the State to individuals described in section 1396a(a)(10)(A)(ii)(V) of this title.

(3) Use of projected income

In applying section 1396b(f)(1) of this title in determining the eligibility of an individual (described in section 1396a(a)(10)(C) of this title) for medical assistance for home and community care, a State may, at its option, provide for the determination of the individual's anticipated medical expenses (to be deducted from income) over a period of up to 6 months.

(c) Determinations of functional disability

(1) In general

In this section, an individual is "functionally disabled" if the individual—

(A) is unable to perform without substantial assistance from another individual at least 2 of the following 3 activities of daily living: toileting, transferring, and eating; or

(B) has a primary or secondary diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease and is (i) unable to perform without substantial human assistance (including verbal reminding or physical cueing) or supervision at least 2 of the following 5 activities of daily living: bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring, and eating; or (ii) cognitively impaired so as to require substantial supervision from another individual because he or she engages in inappropriate behaviors that pose serious health or safety hazards to himself or herself or others.

(2) Assessments of functional disability

(A) Requests for assessments

If a State has elected to provide home and community care under this section, upon the request of an individual who is 65 years of age or older and who meets the requirements of subsection (b)(1)(C) (or another person on such individual's behalf), the State shall provide for a comprehensive functional assessment under this subparagraph which—

(i) is used to determine whether or not the individual is functionally disabled,

(ii) is based on a uniform minimum data set specified by the Secretary under subparagraph (C)(i), and

(iii) uses an instrument which has been specified by the State under subparagraph (B).

No fee may be charged for such an assessment.

(B) Specification of assessment instrument

The State shall specify the instrument to be used in the State in complying with the requirement of subparagraph (A)(iii) which instrument shall be—

(i) one of the instruments designated under subparagraph (C)(ii); or

(ii) an instrument which the Secretary has approved as being consistent with the minimum data set of core elements, common definitions, and utilization guidelines specified by the Secretary in subparagraph (C)(i).

(C) Specification of assessment data set and instruments

The Secretary shall—
