For purposes of this subsection, an urgent medical need means continued enrollment in the BH I/DD Tailored Plan could jeopardize the member's life, physical or mental health, or ability to attain, maintain, or regain maximum function.
The Enrollment Broker will process requests for expedited review in accordance with the following:
The Enrollment Broker will transmit expedited review requests to the Department for evaluation within twelve (12) hours of receipt of the request.

Title: Medical Loss Ratio 15.4
Type: managed_care_contract
Citation link: [Contract--30-190029-DHB-Prepaid-Health-Plan-Services RFP](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-190029-dhb-prepaid-health-plan-services-rfp/download?attachment)

Content:
The CMS Final Rule outlines requirements for rate-setting and financial reporting related to the medical loss ratio (MLR). From a rate-setting standpoint, 42 CFR 438.4(b)(9) stipulates that rates must be established in such a way that a PHP would reasonably achieve a MLR of at least 85%. From a financial reporting perspective, CMS prescribes the MLR calculation methodology in 42 CFR 438.8 for states and their contractors including how to classify various incurred costs and how to develop the numerator and denominator included in the ratio. Lastly, the Final Rule allows, but does not require, states to implement a remittance process for PHPs which do not meet state-established minimum MLR thresholds.

Title: Actuarial soundness
Section: 438.4
Policy: 42-CFR-438
Type: federal_regulation

Federal Register cite: [81 FR 27853, May 6, 2016, as amended at 85 FR 72837, Nov. 13, 2020; 85 FR 72837, Nov. 13, 2020]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

Content:
(a) Actuarially sound capitation rates defined. Actuarially sound capitation rates are projected to provide for all reasonable, appropriate, and attainable costs that are required under the terms of the contract and for the operation of the MCO, PIHP, or PAHP for the time period and the population covered under the terms of the contract, and such capitation rates are developed in accordance with the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section.

(b) CMS review and approval of actuarially sound capitation rates. Capitation rates for MCOs, PIHPs, and PAHPs must be reviewed and approved by CMS as actuarially sound. To be approved by CMS, capitation rates must:

(1) Have been developed in accordance with the standards specified in § 438.5 and generally accepted actuarial principles and practices. Any differences in the assumptions, methodologies, or factors used to develop capitation rates for covered populations must be based on valid rate development standards that represent actual cost differences in providing covered services to the covered populations. Any differences in the assumptions, methodologies, or factors used to develop capitation rates must not vary with the rate of Federal financial participation (FFP) associated with the covered populations in a manner that increases Federal costs. The determination that differences in the assumptions, methodologies, or factors used to develop capitation rates for MCOs, PIHPs, and PAHPs increase Federal costs and vary with the rate of FFP associated with the covered populations must be evaluated for the entire managed care program and include all managed care contracts for all covered populations. CMS may require a State to provide written documentation and justification that any differences in the assumptions, methodologies, or factors used to develop capitation rates for covered populations or contracts represent actual cost differences based on the characteristics and mix of the covered services or the covered populations.

(2) Be appropriate for the populations to be covered and the services to be furnished under the contract.

(3) Be adequate to meet the requirements on MCOs, PIHPs, and PAHPs in §§ 438.206, 438.207, and 438.208.

(4) Be specific to payments for each rate cell under the contract.

(5) Payments from any rate cell must not cross-subsidize or be cross-subsidized by payments for any other rate cell.

(6) Be certified by an actuary as meeting the applicable requirements of this part, including that the rates have been developed in accordance with the requirements specified in § 438.3(c)(1)(ii) and (e).

(7) Meet any applicable special contract provisions as specified in § 438.6.

(8) Be provided to CMS in a format and within a timeframe that meets requirements in § 438.7.

(9) Be developed in such a way that the MCO, PIHP, or PAHP would reasonably achieve a medical loss ratio standard, as calculated under § 438.8, of at least 85 percent for the rate year. The capitation rates may be developed in such a way that the MCO, PIHP, or PAHP would reasonably achieve a medical loss ratio standard greater than 85 percent, as calculated under § 438.8, as long as the capitation rates are adequate for reasonable, appropriate, and attainable non-benefit costs.

(c) Option to develop and certify a rate range. (1) Notwithstanding the provision at paragraph (b)(4) of this section, the State may develop and certify a range of capitation rates per rate cell as actuarially sound, when all of the following conditions are met:

(i) The rate certification identifies and justifies the assumptions, data, and methodologies specific to both the upper and lower bounds of the rate range.

(ii) Both the upper and lower bounds of the rate range must be certified as actuarially sound consistent with the requirements of this part.

(iii) The upper bound of the rate range does not exceed the lower bound of the rate range multiplied by 1.05.

(iv) The rate certification documents the State's criteria for paying MCOs, PIHPs, and PAHPs at different points within the rate range.

(v) The State does not use as a criterion for paying MCOs, PIHPs, and PAHPs at different points within the rate range any of the following:

(A) The willingness or agreement of the MCOs, PIHPs, or PAHPs or their network providers to enter into, or adhere to, intergovernmental transfer (IGT) agreements; or

(B) The amount of funding the MCOs, PIHPs, or PAHPs or their network providers provide through IGT agreements.

(2) When a State develops and certifies a range of capitation rates per rate cell as actuarially sound consistent with the requirements of this paragraph (c), the State must:

(i) Document the capitation rates, prior to the start of the rating period, for the MCOs, PIHPs, and PAHPs at points within the rate range, consistent with the criteria in paragraph (c)(1)(iv) of this section.

(ii) Not modify the capitation rates under § 438.7(c)(3).

(iii) Not modify the capitation rates within the rate range, unless the State is increasing or decreasing the capitation rate per rate cell within the rate range up to 1 percent during the rating period. However, any changes of the capitation rate within the permissible 1 percent range must be consistent with a modification of the contract as required in § 438.3(c) and are subject to the requirements at paragraph (b)(1) of this section. Any modification to the capitation rates within the rate range greater than the permissible 1 percent range will require the State to provide a revised rate certification for CMS approval, which demonstrates that—

(A) The criteria in paragraph (c)(1)(iv) of this section, as described in the initial rate certification, were not applied accurately;

(B) There was a material error in the data, assumptions, or methodologies used to develop the initial rate certification and that the modifications are necessary to correct the error; or

per_question.question: When does NC Medicaid pay for CAR-T cell treatment? What specific criteria have to be met?
per_question.agent_answer:
NC Medicaid pays for CAR-T cell therapy when it is **medically necessary** and **all policy-specific coverage criteria are met** under current Clinical Coverage Policy 11A-17, effective April 1, 2025. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment) [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

## Required coverage criteria

NC Medicaid covers CAR-T cell therapy only if the service is **medically necessary**. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

In addition, the therapy must be **individualized, specific, and consistent with the beneficiary’s symptoms or confirmed diagnosis**, and it cannot be more than the beneficiary needs. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

It also must be a service that **can be safely furnished**, and there must be **no equally effective and more conservative or less costly treatment available statewide**. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

The service also cannot be furnished primarily for the **convenience of the beneficiary, caretaker, or provider**. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

Beyond those general rules, Medicaid covers CAR-T cell therapy only when **all** of these specific conditions are met: the CAR-T therapy has **FDA approval**; it is administered in accordance with **FDA-approved guidelines** for indications and usage, dosage and administration, dosage forms and strengths, and warnings and precautions; and it is given at a **certified or authorized treatment center**. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

If the CAR-T product is subject to a **REMS program**, the treatment center must be **enrolled in the REMS**, and providers must be **trained to manage cytokine release syndrome and neurologic toxicities**. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

The policy states there are **no additional Medicaid-specific covered criteria** beyond those listed above. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

## Situations where Medicaid will not pay

NC Medicaid does **not** cover CAR-T therapy if the product **does not have FDA approval**. [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

It also does **not** cover CAR-T therapy if it is given **outside FDA guidelines** for indications and usage, dosage and administration, or dosage forms and strengths. [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

If a CAR-T therapy requires a **REMS**, Medicaid will not cover it when it is administered at a facility that **is not enrolled** in that REMS program. [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

Medicaid also will not cover **repeat treatment** for a beneficiary who previously received another CAR-T therapy. [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

Coverage is excluded when the beneficiary’s **psychosocial history limits the ability to comply** with required pre- and post-infusion care, or when there is **current beneficiary or caretaker non-compliance** making adherence to a disciplined medical regimen improbable. [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

NC Medicaid also does not cover a **concurrent rescue transplant with infusion of any CAR-T therapy**, because the policy considers that **experimental**. [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

## Prior approval

CAR-T cell therapy requires **prior approval** from Medicaid before the provider renders the service. [Policy 11A-17 § 5.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

## Bottom line

A practical summary is that NC Medicaid will pay for CAR-T treatment when it is **medically necessary, FDA-approved, used exactly within FDA-approved parameters, delivered at the proper certified/authorized center, and—if applicable—handled through a REMS-enrolled facility with appropriately trained providers**. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment) [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

If you want, I can also turn this into a **checklist for a prior authorization request** or identify **what records a provider should submit to show each criterion is met**.

scores.explanation: The agent's answer accurately captures all key criteria from Policy 11A-17: general medical necessity criteria (§3.1), specific coverage criteria including FDA approval, FDA-guideline compliance, certified treatment center, and REMS requirements (§3.2.1), non-coverage criteria (§4.2.1 and §4.2.2), and prior approval requirement (§5.1). All claims are directly supported by the evidence blocks. Citations are precise and section-level. The answer is comprehensive, well-organized, and would be fully acceptable to a Medicaid policy expert.

per_question.question: Up to what age can children on Medicaid receive fluoride varnish from their physician, and what oral screening has to accompany it?
per_question.agent_answer:
Children can receive physician-applied fluoride varnish from tooth eruption until age 3½ under NC Medicaid’s physician fluoride varnish policy, and Medicaid covers up to six oral screening packages during that period. Each package includes an oral evaluation/examination, preventive oral health and dietary counseling, and application of fluoride varnish.

The oral screening that must accompany it is an early caries screening and detection of notable findings in the oral cavity using a dental mirror and directed light. The policy also requires documentation of an oral evaluation and any notable findings, preventive oral health and dietary counseling with the primary caregiver, and application of fluoride varnish.

The current policy text in the corpus shows Amended Date: April 1, 2023, and the latest listed change notice says the policy was revised effective April 1, 2023.

If you want, I can also pull the exact billing-code pairing for the oral evaluation and varnish.

---

*Suggested citations for uncited claims above:*
- [Policy 1A-23 § 3.2.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1a-23-physician-fluoride-varnish-services/download?attachment)
- [Policy 1A-23 § 7.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1a-23-physician-fluoride-varnish-services/download?attachment)
- [Policy 1A-23](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1a-23-physician-fluoride-varnish-services/download?attachment)

All claims are supported by the Evidence block (sections 3.2.2, 5.3.1, and 7.2). No hallucinations are present. The amendment date (April 1, 2023) is confirmed in the evidence. Citations reference specific policy sections (§3.2.2 and §7.2) which is reasonably precise, though the inline citation links are somewhat generic URLs rather than pinpointed section anchors. Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) is a federal Medicaid requirement that requires the state Medicaid agency to cover services, products, or procedures for Medicaid beneficiary under 21 years of age if the service is medically necessary health care to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition [health problem] identified through a screening examination (includes any evaluation by a physician or other licensed practitioner).
This means EPSDT covers most of the medical or remedial care a child needs to improve or maintain his or her health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.
Medically necessary services will be provided in the most economic mode, as long as the treatment made available is similarly efficacious to the service requested by the beneficiary's physician, therapist, or other licensed practitioner; the determination process does not delay the delivery of the needed service; and the determination does not limit the beneficiary's right to a free choice of providers.
EPSDT does not require the state Medicaid agency to provide any service, product or procedure:
that is unsafe, ineffective, or experimental or investigational.
that is not medical in nature or not generally recognized as an accepted method of medical practice or treatment.
Service limitations on scope, amount, duration, frequency, location of service, and other specific criteria described in clinical coverage policies may be exceeded or may not apply as long as the provider's documentation shows that the requested service is medically necessary 'to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition' [health problem]; that is, provider documentation shows how the service, product, or procedure meets all EPSDT criteria, including to correct or improve or maintain the beneficiary's health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.

per_question.question: An NC Innovations participant's needs cost more than their individual base budget. Can they request services beyond the budget, and what recourse do they have if they think the budget can't meet their needs?
per_question.agent_answer:
Yes. An NC Innovations participant may request services that cost more than their base budget if they believe their needs cannot be met within that budget , and the policy says the SIS results and base budget are only guidelines rather than a binding cap on what may be requested or authorized . If the LME/MCO determines the requested services are medically necessary, they must be authorized regardless of the base budget .

The policy also says no change in the amount of the budget is needed in order to approve services in excess of the budget .

If the participant thinks the budget cannot meet their needs, they can ask for authorization of services above the base budget based on medical necessity . If a SIS update results in a higher budget, the individual can work with the planning team to update the ISP for increased services, and the Care Coordinator will submit the updated ISP to UM for approval . If any request for authorization of services is denied, the LME/MCO must tell the individual the reasons for the decision and how to appeal , and the individual may file a grievance regarding the base budget .

The policy also states that the individual budget is not a binding limit, but combined base-budget and non-base-budget services may not total more than the $135,000 waiver cost limit unless the listed exception criteria are met .

---

*Suggested citations for uncited claims above:*
- [Clinical Coverage Policy 8-P, North Carolina Innovations](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8-p-north-carolina-innovations/download?attachment)

All claims are directly supported by the evidence blocks (sections _s564, _s565, _s560). ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8P:_s564
Title: Category Assignment and Individual Budget Changes
Policy: 8P
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 8-P, North Carolina Innovations](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8-p-north-carolina-innovations/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched category.
Content:
A Level is assigned every person on the NC Innovations Waiver. This level is based on the Support Intensity Scale ('SIS') which is the assessment instrument used to measure individual support needs.
The SIS scores are uploaded to SIS On-line with AAIDD.  Within 15 calendar days of receiving notice that the SIS has been uploaded, NC Medicaid, or their designee, applies the algorithm and assigns an initial level and individual budget.  If a SIS is updated, the results of the SIS may indicate a change in the level of support needs.  This may result in a new Individual Budget Tool Level and base budget being assigned. Within thirty (30) calendar days of a SIS being performed and NC Medicaid, or their designee's notification, NC Medicaid, or their designee will determine if there has been a Level change and the LME/MCO will notify the beneficiary in writing within 15 days of receiving notice from NC Medicaid, or their designee.  The beneficiary will also be notified if there is not a Level change.  A Level change may not always result in a change in the beneficiary's base budget, but the beneficiary will always be notified if there is a Level change and budget change.
If the beneficiary's level change has resulted in an increase in budget, that budget increase can take effect sixty (60) calendar days from the date on the letter. During that sixty (60) calendar day period, the individual can develop an update to his/her Individual Support Plan ('ISP') with the planning team allowing for the increased services, if they choose. The Care Coordinator will submit an updated ISP to UM for approval. If the beneficiary's Level change has resulted in a decrease in budget, the budget decrease will take effect at the end of the individual's most recently approved Annual ISP. No currently authorized services will be reduced as a result of the budget change. The letters notifying the individual of the decrease in budget will notify the individual of the following:
He or she may request services that cost in excess of his or her base budget if he or she believes his or her needs cannot be met within his or her base budget; and
The results of the SIS and the base budget are guidelines that do not constitute a binding limit on the amount of services that may be requested or authorized, and if the LME/MCO determines services to be medically necessary, they will be authorized, regardless of the base budget.
If any request for authorization of services is denied, the LME/MCO will notify the individual of the reasons for the decision and how to appeal
How to file a grievance regarding the base budget if he or she wishes to do so.

Policy: 8P
Type: clinical_policy

Content:
Sometimes, an individual's support needs may not be met in his or her assigned level base budget.  If Utilization Management determines requested services to be medically necessary, they will be authorized.
There are a variety of ways for a beneficiary's base budget to be modified. However, no change in the amount of the budget is needed in order to approve services in excess of the budget.

Content:
The Individual Budget is only one measure of a beneficiary's likely current needs and is not a binding limit on the amount of funding for any period of time. The Individual Budget is reviewed no less frequently than annually by the PIHP. The Individual Budget includes only Base Budget Services. NonBase Budget services are not included. Base Budget services are the core habilitation and support services in the waiver. Non-Base Budget services are preventative services, and equipment. Combined these services may not total more than the $135,000 cost limit within the waiver unless the follow criteria is met:
An individual may exceed the $135,000 waiver limit, to ensure health, safety and wellbeing, if the following criteria is met:
Beneficiaries utilizing Supported Living Level III:
lives independently without his or her family in a home that s/he owns, rents or leases, and
receives Supported Living Level III, and
requires 24 hour support.

Content:
Medicaid
Clinical Coverage Policy No: 8-P
Amended Date: April 1, 2023
Monitoring takes place in all service settings and on a schedule outlined in the ISP.
The Care Coordinator is responsible for monitoring the ISP, and reviews goals at a minimum frequency based on the target date assigned to each goal. Goals may be, and often are, reviewed more frequently, based on the needs of the beneficiary.  The Care Coordinator also maintains close contact with the beneficiary, the legally responsible person or parent or guardian (if applicable), providers, and other members of the person-centered planning team, noting any recommended revisions needed.  This ensures that changes are noted, and updates are effectuated in a timely manner.
Monitoring methods also consist of contacts (face-to-face and telephone calls) with other members of the ISP team and review of service documentation. A standard monitoring checklist is used to ensure that the following issues are monitored:
Verification that services are provided as outlined in the ISP;
The beneficiary has access to services;
Identification of any problems that may arise;
The services meet the needs of the beneficiary;
The back-up staffing plans are documented;
Issues of health and welfare (rights restrictions, medical care, abuse, neglect or exploitation, behavior support plan) are addressed;
That the beneficiary has been offered a free choice of providers; and
That non-waiver services needs have been addressed.
Care Coordinator monitoring occurs monthly and consists of the following:
A beneficiary that is new to the waiver receives face-to-face visits for the first six months and then on a schedule agreed to by the ISP team thereafter, no less than quarterly, to meet their health and safety needs;
A beneficiary whose services are provided by guardians and relatives living in the home of the beneficiary receives monthly face-to-face monitoring visits;
A beneficiary who lives in residential programs receives face-to-face monitoring visits monthly;
A beneficiary who chooses the individual family-directed service option receives face-to-face monitoring visits monthly;
For the months that the beneficiary does not receive face-to-face monitoring, the Care Coordinator has telephone contact with the beneficiary to ensure that there are no issues that need to be addressed;
At least one service is utilized monthly, per waiver eligibility requirements;
NC Innovations services utilized do not exceed authorization.  If there is an emergency, the Care Coordinator shall ensure that beneficiary's needs are met and ensure that any updates to the LOC and ISP, based upon the changes in needs of the beneficiary, are processed in a timely manner; and
Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) rules are met. Any concerns noted by the Care Coordinator regarding HCBS (such as privacy, restriction
of rights, access to food) must be reported to the PIHP. Any restrictions to HCBS must be addressed in the ISP.

ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-435:435.121
Title: Individuals in States using more restrictive requirements for Medicaid than the SSI requirements
Section: 435.121
Policy: 42-CFR-435
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2013-07-15
Federal Register cite: [58 FR 4926, Jan. 19, 1993, as amended at 78 FR 42302, July 15, 2013]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-435)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
(a) Basic eligibility group requirements. (1) If the agency does not provide Medicaid under § 435.120 to aged, blind, and disabled individuals who are SSI beneficiaries, the agency must provide Medicaid to aged, blind, and disabled individuals who meet eligibility requirements that are specified in this section.

(2) Except to the extent provided in paragraph (a)(3) of this section, the agency may elect to apply more restrictive eligibility requirements to the aged, blind, and disabled that are more restrictive than those of the SSI program. The more restrictive requirements may be no more restrictive than those requirements contained in the State's Medicaid plan in effect on January 1, 1972. If any of the State's 1972 Medicaid plan requirements were more liberal than of the SSI program, the State must use the SSI requirement instead of the more liberal requirements, except to the extent the State elects to use more liberal criteria under § 435.601.

(3) The agency must not apply a more restrictive requirement under the provisions of paragraph (a)(2) of this section if:

(i) The requirement conflicts with the requirements of section 1924 of the Act, which governs the eligibility and post-eligibility treatment of income and resources of institutionalized individuals with community spouses;

(ii) The requirement conflicts with a more liberal requirement which the agency has elected to use under § 435.601; or

(iii) The more restrictive requirement conflicts with a more liberal requirement the State has elected to use under § 435.234(c) in determining eligibility for State supplementary payments.

(b) Mandatory coverage. If the agency chooses to apply more restrictive requirements than SSI to aged, blind, or disabled individuals, it must provide Medicaid to:

(1) Individuals who meet the requirements of section 1619(b)(3) of the Act even though they may not continue to meet the requirements of this section; and

(2) Qualified Medicare beneficiaries described in section 1905(p) of the Act and qualified working disabled individuals described in section 1905(s) of the Act without consideration of the more restrictive eligibility requirements specified in this section.

(3) Individuals who:

(i) Qualify for benefits under section 1619(a) or are in eligibility status under section 1619(b)(1) of the Act as determined by SSA; and

(ii) Were eligible for Medicaid under the more restrictive criteria in the State's approved Medicaid plan in the reference month—the month immediately preceding the first month in which they became eligible under section 1619(a) or (b)(1) of the Act. “Were eligible for Medicaid” means that individuals were issued Medicaid cards by the State for the reference month. Under this provision, the reference month for determining Medicaid eligibility for all individuals under section 1619 of the Act is the month immediately preceding the first month of the most recent period of eligibility under section 1619 of the Act.

(c) Group composition. The agency may apply more restrictive requirements only to the aged, to the blind, to the disabled, or to any combination of these groups. For example, the agency may apply more restrictive requirements to the aged and disabled under this provision and provide Medicaid to all blind individuals who are SSI beneficiaries.

(d) Nonfinancial conditions. The agency may apply more restrictive requirements that are nonfinancial conditions of eligibility. For example, the agency may use a more restrictive definition of disability or may limit eligibility of the disabled to individuals age 18 and older, or both. If the agency limits eligibility of disabled individuals to individuals age 18 or older, it must provide Medicaid to individuals under age 18 who receive SSI benefits and who would be eligible to receive AFDC under the State's approved plan if they did not receive SSI. If the agency imposed an age limit for disabled individuals under its 1972 approved State plan but does not use that limit, it must apply the same nonfinancial requirement to individuals under age 18 that it applies to disabled individuals age 18 and older.

(e) Financial conditions. (1) The agency may apply more restrictive requirements that are financial conditions of eligibility.

(2) Any income eligibility standards that the agency applies must:

(i) Equal the income standard (or Federal Benefit Rate (FBR)) that would be used under SSI based on an individual's living arrangement; or

(ii) Be a more restrictive standard which is no more restrictive than that under the approved State's January 1, 1972 Medicaid plan.

(3) If the categorically needy income standard established under paragraph (e)(2) of this section is less than the optional categorically needy standard established under § 435.230, the agency must provide Medicaid to all aged, blind, and disabled individuals who have income equal to or below the higher standard.

(4) In a State that does not have a medically needy program that covers aged, blind, and disabled individuals, the agency must allow individuals to deduct from income incurred medical and remedial expenses (that is, spend down) to become eligible under this section. However, individuals with income above the categorically needy standards may only spend down to the standard selected by the State under paragraph (e)(2) of this section which applies to the individual's living arrangement.

(5) In a State that elects to provide medically needy coverage to aged, blind, and disabled individuals, the agency must allow individuals to deduct from income incurred medical and remedial care expenses (spend down) to become categorically needy when they are SSI beneficiaries (including individuals deemed to be SSI beneficiaries under §§ 435.135, 435.137, and 435.138), eligible spouses of SSI beneficiaries, State supplement beneficiaries, and individuals who are eligible for a supplement but who do not receive supplementary payments. All Requests for Community Living and Supports require prior approval by the PIHP:
Requests for up to 12 hours daily may be authorized for the entire plan year.
Requests for up to 16 hours daily may be authorized for a six-month timeframe, within the plan year.
Requests for more than 16 hours daily are authorized for up to a 90-day period within the plan year. In situations requiring an authorization beyond the initial 90-day period, the PIHP shall approve such authorization based on review of Medical Necessity. The treatment team should meet to review individuals' status and identify sustainable supports, if available and information from the meeting should be included in the individual's ISP.  Review of other options should include options within the Innovations Waiver, as well as options outside of the Innovations waiver such as Medicaid State Plan Services.
The service may be provided in the home or community. The involvement of unpaid supports in the generalization of the service is an important aspect to ensure that achieved goals are practiced and maintained.  Services may be allowed in the private home of the provider or staff of an Employer of Record at the discretion and agreement of the support team and when consistent with the ISP goals. If services are provided in the primary residence of the provider or staff of the employer of record, the Health and Safety Checklist must be completed before service begins and every six months thereafter.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8P:_s564
Title: Category Assignment and Individual Budget Changes
Policy: 8P
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2016-11-01
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 8-P, North Carolina Innovations](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8-p-north-carolina-innovations/download?attachment)

Content:
A Level is assigned every person on the NC Innovations Waiver. This level is based on the Support Intensity Scale ('SIS') which is the assessment instrument used to measure individual support needs.
The SIS scores are uploaded to SIS On-line with AAIDD.  Within 15 calendar days of receiving notice that the SIS has been uploaded, NC Medicaid, or their designee, applies the algorithm and assigns an initial level and individual budget.  If a SIS is updated, the results of the SIS may indicate a change in the level of support needs.  This may result in a new Individual Budget Tool Level and base budget being assigned. Within thirty (30) calendar days of a SIS being performed and NC Medicaid, or their designee's notification, NC Medicaid, or their designee will determine if there has been a Level change and the LME/MCO will notify the beneficiary in writing within 15 days of receiving notice from NC Medicaid, or their designee.  The beneficiary will also be notified if there is not a Level change.  A Level change may not always result in a change in the beneficiary's base budget, but the beneficiary will always be notified if there is a Level change and budget change.
If the beneficiary's level change has resulted in an increase in budget, that budget increase can take effect sixty (60) calendar days from the date on the letter. During that sixty (60) calendar day period, the individual can develop an update to his/her Individual Support Plan ('ISP') with the planning team allowing for the increased services, if they choose. The Care Coordinator will submit an updated ISP to UM for approval. If the beneficiary's Level change has resulted in a decrease in budget, the budget decrease will take effect at the end of the individual's most recently approved Annual ISP. No currently authorized services will be reduced as a result of the budget change. The letters notifying the individual of the decrease in budget will notify the individual of the following:
He or she may request services that cost in excess of his or her base budget if he or she believes his or her needs cannot be met within his or her base budget; and
The results of the SIS and the base budget are guidelines that do not constitute a binding limit on the amount of services that may be requested or authorized, and if the LME/MCO determines services to be medically necessary, they will be authorized, regardless of the base budget.
If any request for authorization of services is denied, the LME/MCO will notify the individual of the reasons for the decision and how to appeal
How to file a grievance regarding the base budget if he or she wishes to do so.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8P:_s565
Title: Changes within the Individual Budget Tool
Policy: 8P
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2016-11-01
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 8-P, North Carolina Innovations](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8-p-north-carolina-innovations/download?attachment)

Content:
Sometimes, an individual's support needs may not be met in his or her assigned level base budget.  If Utilization Management determines requested services to be medically necessary, they will be authorized.
There are a variety of ways for a beneficiary's base budget to be modified. However, no change in the amount of the budget is needed in order to approve services in excess of the budget.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8P:_s560
Title: Components of the Individual Budgeting Tool
Policy: 8P
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2016-11-01
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 8-P, North Carolina Innovations](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8-p-north-carolina-innovations/download?attachment)

Content:
The Individual Budget is only one measure of a beneficiary's likely current needs and is not a binding limit on the amount of funding for any period of time. The Individual Budget is reviewed no less frequently than annually by the PIHP. The Individual Budget includes only Base Budget Services. NonBase Budget services are not included. Base Budget services are the core habilitation and support services in the waiver. Non-Base Budget services are preventative services, and equipment. Combined these services may not total more than the $135,000 cost limit within the waiver unless the follow criteria is met:
An individual may exceed the $135,000 waiver limit, to ensure health, safety and wellbeing, if the following criteria is met:
Beneficiaries utilizing Supported Living Level III:
lives independently without his or her family in a home that s/he owns, rents or leases, and
receives Supported Living Level III, and
requires 24 hour support.

ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-435:435.121
Title: Individuals in States using more restrictive requirements for Medicaid than the SSI requirements
Section: 435.121
Policy: 42-CFR-435
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2013-07-15
Federal Register cite: [58 FR 4926, Jan. 19, 1993, as amended at 78 FR 42302, July 15, 2013]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-435)

Content:
(a) Basic eligibility group requirements. (1) If the agency does not provide Medicaid under § 435.120 to aged, blind, and disabled individuals who are SSI beneficiaries, the agency must provide Medicaid to aged, blind, and disabled individuals who meet eligibility requirements that are specified in this section.

(2) Except to the extent provided in paragraph (a)(3) of this section, the agency may elect to apply more restrictive eligibility requirements to the aged, blind, and disabled that are more restrictive than those of the SSI program. The more restrictive requirements may be no more restrictive than those requirements contained in the State's Medicaid plan in effect on January 1, 1972. If any of the State's 1972 Medicaid plan requirements were more liberal than of the SSI program, the State must use the SSI requirement instead of the more liberal requirements, except to the extent the State elects to use more liberal criteria under § 435.601.

(3) The agency must not apply a more restrictive requirement under the provisions of paragraph (a)(2) of this section if:

(i) The requirement conflicts with the requirements of section 1924 of the Act, which governs the eligibility and post-eligibility treatment of income and resources of institutionalized individuals with community spouses;

(ii) The requirement conflicts with a more liberal requirement which the agency has elected to use under § 435.601; or

(iii) The more restrictive requirement conflicts with a more liberal requirement the State has elected to use under § 435.234(c) in determining eligibility for State supplementary payments.

(b) Mandatory coverage. If the agency chooses to apply more restrictive requirements than SSI to aged, blind, or disabled individuals, it must provide Medicaid to:

(1) Individuals who meet the requirements of section 1619(b)(3) of the Act even though they may not continue to meet the requirements of this section; and

(2) Qualified Medicare beneficiaries described in section 1905(p) of the Act and qualified working disabled individuals described in section 1905(s) of the Act without consideration of the more restrictive eligibility requirements specified in this section.

(3) Individuals who:

(i) Qualify for benefits under section 1619(a) or are in eligibility status under section 1619(b)(1) of the Act as determined by SSA; and

(ii) Were eligible for Medicaid under the more restrictive criteria in the State's approved Medicaid plan in the reference month—the month immediately preceding the first month in which they became eligible under section 1619(a) or (b)(1) of the Act. “Were eligible for Medicaid” means that individuals were issued Medicaid cards by the State for the reference month. Under this provision, the reference month for determining Medicaid eligibility for all individuals under section 1619 of the Act is the month immediately preceding the first month of the most recent period of eligibility under section 1619 of the Act.

(c) Group composition. The agency may apply more restrictive requirements only to the aged, to the blind, to the disabled, or to any combination of these groups. For example, the agency may apply more restrictive requirements to the aged and disabled under this provision and provide Medicaid to all blind individuals who are SSI beneficiaries.

(d) Nonfinancial conditions. The agency may apply more restrictive requirements that are nonfinancial conditions of eligibility. For example, the agency may use a more restrictive definition of disability or may limit eligibility of the disabled to individuals age 18 and older, or both. If the agency limits eligibility of disabled individuals to individuals age 18 or older, it must provide Medicaid to individuals under age 18 who receive SSI benefits and who would be eligible to receive AFDC under the State's approved plan if they did not receive SSI. If the agency imposed an age limit for disabled individuals under its 1972 approved State plan but does not use that limit, it must apply the same nonfinancial requirement to individuals under age 18 that it applies to disabled individuals age 18 and older.

(2) Any income eligibility standards that the agency applies must:

(i) Equal the income standard (or Federal Benefit Rate (FBR)) that would be used under SSI based on an individual's living arrangement; or

(ii) Be a more restrictive standard which is no more restrictive than that under the approved State's January 1, 1972 Medicaid plan.

per_question.question: What does it take to become a certified HIV case management provider for NC Medicaid, and what circumstances can lead to a provider losing that certification?
per_question.agent_answer:
To become a certified HIV Case Management provider for NC Medicaid, an agency must obtain certification from NC Medicaid or its designated contractor before enrollment, meet provider-agency and staffing standards in Policy 12B, submit a complete initial certification application, and then maintain those standards through recertification and ongoing compliance.

## What it takes to become certified

An agency must obtain certification from NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor, to be considered for enrollment with NC Medicaid as an HIV Case Management provider. [Policy 12B § 6.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

To qualify for reimbursement, the provider must have a documented successful record of three years providing or managing HIV Case Management programs.

The provider must ensure services are furnished by qualified HIV case managers and supervised by qualified supervisors meeting the policy’s staff-qualification standards.

Each physical site must be enrolled with NC Medicaid as an HIV Case Management provider.

The provider must meet applicable state and federal Medicaid participation laws, maintain certification, comply with initial and ongoing certification processes, maintain a quality improvement plan for monitoring and evaluating case-management records, allow record and operational review, and notify NC Medicaid or its designated contractor of proposed ownership, name, address, telephone, or dissolution changes within the policy deadlines.

Within one year of Medicaid enrollment, the provider must achieve national accreditation from at least one designated accrediting body: ACHC, CARF, CHAP, COA, PHAB, The Joint Commission, or URAC.

A provider is ineligible for certification if it has previously been decertified as an HIV Case Management agency, if its provider number has been suspended because of Program Integrity sanctions, or if it has failed to repay money owed to the North Carolina Medicaid program.

### Staff qualification requirements

An HIV case manager must meet one of the educational or licensure pathways listed in the policy and, in addition, must have two years of case-management experience and possess or acquire a clinical understanding of HIV documented in the personnel file.

The policy defines acceptable case-management experience to include intake, assessment, reassessment, care planning, case coordination, case conferencing, care-plan implementation, referral, linkage and resource development, crisis intervention, monitoring and follow-up, and discharge or termination.

A supervisor must meet one of the policy’s education or licensure pathways and must also have three years of case-management experience.

All HIV case managers and supervisors must complete North Carolina state-sponsored basic training within 90 days of employment and before any billed case-management units.

All HIV case managers and supervisors must also complete 12 hours of HIV Case Management continuing education annually, and six of those hours must be clinically oriented.

The provider is responsible for verifying staff qualifications and credentials before hiring and ensuring continued compliance during employment, and it must keep verification of staff credentials.

### Application and documentation expectations

For initial certification, the provider must submit a complete and signed application, and the initial certification is valid for one year.

The recertification materials show the kind of information NC Medicaid expects agencies to maintain and submit, including staff names and hire dates, counties served, services offered, hours of operation, an emergency after-hours plan, accreditation information, satisfaction-survey practices, and counts of Medicaid and Ryan White clients.

The checklist also requires attached policies and supporting documents including confidentiality, grievance, beneficiary rights, nondiscrimination, code of ethics, conflict of interest, electronic records, Medicaid record retention, freedom of choice, transfer and discharge, abuse/neglect/exploitation, quality assurance materials, organizational chart, community resources, ownership information, staff credentials, CCNC/PCP networking, and HR policies, procedures, and plans.

The recertification application requires the agency to agree that Medicaid may review beneficiary records and other HIV Case Management information, that the provider will submit to an on-site recertification visit, that it will provide regular supervision by a qualified supervisor, that it will maintain a business plan and computer capabilities to comply with policy mandates, and that it will comply with applicable laws including HIPAA and record-retention requirements.

## Ongoing recertification

Recertification is valid for two years unless otherwise specified.

To be recertified, the provider must submit a complete and signed recertification application within 60 calendar days of receipt, copies of items from the initial-certification package that have changed, copies of HIV case manager and supervisor credentials, annual summaries of quality-improvement activities with outcome metrics, and it must submit to an on-site recertification visit with review of beneficiary records or other clinical and business documentation as needed.

If the recertification application does not meet the criteria after 90 days, it is returned as incomplete and NC Medicaid or its designated contractor need take no further action.

If site visits show noncompliance, NC Medicaid or its designated contractor may issue a provisional recertification for six months to allow monitoring.

## What can cause a provider to lose certification

NC Medicaid or its designated contractor is responsible for decertifying agencies that fail to render services in accordance with professionally recognized standards and the policy.

A provider may be decertified and disenrolled if any listed ground is substantiated, and the policy says the list is not all-inclusive.

The listed grounds include: failure to provide core service components; fraudulent billing practices; owner convictions for felonies; failure to develop, submit, and implement a written plan of correction within 30 calendar days; falsification of records; violation of a beneficiary's confidentiality; employing staff who do not meet the criteria in the policy; failure of staff to complete mandatory basic training within 90 days; failure of staff to obtain required continuing education; failure to provide staff supervision sufficient to meet beneficiaries’ needs; failure to submit required documentation on time; failure to maintain documentation sufficient to support billing; failure to implement and enforce a quality improvement program; failure to timely notify NC Medicaid or its designated contractor of agency changes causing inability to contact the provider; failure to comply with applicable federal and state laws, regulations, the state reimbursement plan, and governing Medicaid policies; failure to enroll any beneficiaries within four months of certification; and failure to achieve or maintain the certification requirements defined in Policy 12B.

When NC Medicaid or its designated agent notifies a Medicaid-enrolled provider that it is no longer certified to provide HIV Case Management, the provider may request reconsideration review under 10A NCAC 22F.0402.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.5
Title: 6.1.5 Case Management Supervisor's Experience
Section: 6.1.5
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched documentation.
Content:
Case management experience must encompass the functions of intake, assessment, reassessment, care planning, case coordination, case conferencing, care plan implementation, referral, linkage and resource development, crisis intervention, monitoring and follow -up of services provided and discharge or termination.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
In addition to those listed for the CM, the case management supervisor must possess and demonstrate the following knowledge, skills and abilities:
Ability to direct and evaluate the scope and quality of case management services;
Knowledgeable in case management principals, procedures and practices;
Ability to conduct detailed analytical evaluations and studies, and prepare related reports and recommendations; and
Apply professional level of knowledge of federal and state assistance programs for HIV positive population.
The provider shall identify the HIV CM program supervisor within the organization. The supervisor is to provide supervision that addresses both the clinical and professional aspects of the CM's job performance. This is defined as providing regularly scheduled assistance by a qualified professional to a staff member who is working directly with beneficiaries.
The purpose of clinical supervision is to ensure that each beneficiary receives case management services which are consistent with accepted standards of practice and the needs of the beneficiary and care plan.
Documentation of supervisory review of CM's caseload and proper utilization of case management services is required. The supervisor shall attest to the accuracy of the documentation by a personal signature to include credentials and title. Each beneficiary record must reflect supervisory review every 4 weeks at a minimum. The frequency of the reviews must be increased if the findings warrant such action. The review must include the following: the beneficiary record to assure that all required paperwork as defined by this policy is in the record and progress notes must be reviewed for compliance with the requirements in Subsections 7.5 and 7.6. The billing must be checked for accuracy to assure it corresponds to the progress notes. This is not billable case management time.

If any one of the following conditions is substantiated, the provider may be decertified by NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor, and dis-enrolled by NC Medicaid. This list is not all inclusive.
Failure to provide core service components.
Fraudulent billing practices.
Owner(s) being convicted of a felony charge.
Failure to develop, submit, and implement a written plan of correction to resolve unmet program requirements cited by NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor; to make recommended corrections; or both within 30 calendar days.
Falsification of records.
Violation of a beneficiary's confidentiality.
Employment of staff who do not meet the criteria stated in Subsection 6.1.
Failure of staff to complete NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor, mandatory basic training within 90 days of their employment date.
Failure of staff to obtain required continuing educational units (CEU), as specified in Subsection 6.1.
Failure to provide case management staff with supervision to meet the beneficiaries' needs.
Failure to submit any required documentation within the time frame designated by this policy, NC Medicaid or DHHS designated contractor, or both.
Failure to provide documentation as specified in Subsection 7.5 that is sufficient to support the provider's billing.
Failure to implement and enforce a quality improvement program.
Failure to notify NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor, within 30 calendar days of proposed changes, or five business days of actual changes, of any changes in agency name, director or ownership, mailing address, and telephone number(s), resulting in NC Medicaid or DHHS designated contractors, inability to contact the provider.
Failure to comply with all applicable federal and state laws, regulations, state reimbursement plan, and policies governing the services authorized under the Medicaid program.
Failure of a provider to enroll any beneficiaries within four months of certification.
Failure of a provider to achieve or maintain the requirements for certification as defined in Subsection 6.2 of this policy.
When NC Medicaid, or NC Medicaid's designated agent, notifies a Medicaidenrolled provider that he is no longer certified to provide HIV Case Management services, the provider may request a reconsideration review in accordance with 10A NCAC 22F.0402.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.7.1
Title: 6.1.7.1 Training for Case Managers and Supervisors
Section: 6.1.7.1
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched documentation.
Content:
All HIV case managers and case management supervisors shall complete North Carolina state-sponsored, basic training within 90 days of their employment date, and must be completed prior to any billed case management units. It is the responsibility of providers to retain copies of certificates of completion issued by NC Medicaid or DHHS designated contractor.
Upon successful completion of basic training, the CM or supervisor will be able to perform all the following:
describe basic HIV information and prevention techniques;
describe the scope of work for CMs;
identify and explain the core components of HIV Case Management;
demonstrate an understanding of basic ethical issues relating to case management;
demonstrate an understanding of the responsibilities and functions of the HIV CM system of care; and
demonstrate an understanding of the documentation requirements of this program as defined in Subsections 7.5 and 7.6 .

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1
Title: 6.1 Provider Qualifications and Occupational Licensing Entity Regulations
Section: 6.1
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2020-01-15
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Content:
The following actions, taken by NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor, shall render a provider ineligible for certification as a provider of HIV Case Management.
previous actions taken to decertify agency as a provider of HIV Case Management.
provider number suspended as a result of sanctions imposed by Program Integrity.
failure to repay any monies owed to the North Carolina Medicaid program.
It is the responsibility of the provider to verify staff qualifications and credentials prior to hiring and assure, during their employment, that the staff member continues to meet the requirements set forth in this policy. Verification of staff credentials must be maintained by the provider.

Title: 6.2.2 Certification and Decertification Process
Section: 6.2.2
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2020-01-15
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Content:
NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor, is responsible for certifying qualified HIV Case Management providers to render services in accordance with professionally recognized standards, and as specified by this policy, and also for
decertifying those HIV Case Management agencies that fail to render services in accordance with professionally recognized standards, and as specified by this policy.

Section: 6.2.3
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2020-01-15
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Content:
A provider shall comply with all the requirements specified below. The initial certification is valid for one year. Submit a complete and signed application to NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor, that includes the following information as identified under Administrative, Case Management and Human Resource Requirements.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.2.4
Title: 6.2.4 Recertification
Section: 6.2.4
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2020-01-15
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Content:
The recertification is valid for two years, unless otherwise specified. To be recertified, a provider shall:
Submit a complete and signed Recertification Application to NC Medicaid or DHHS designated contractor, within 60 calendar days of receipt.
Submit copies of all items in Subsection 6.2.3 that have changed since the initial certification.
Submit copies of all HIV CM and supervisor credentials.
Submit annual summary, or summaries, of quality improvement activities to include outcome metrics.
Submit to a recertification on-site visit, including a review of beneficiary records or other clinical and business documentation as needed.
Applications that do not meet the above criteria after 90 days will be returned to the agency as incomplete and no further action shall be required by NC Medicaid, DHHS designated contractor.
Note: NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor, shall provide a provisional recertification for a period of six months, if site visits show evidence of noncompliance with policy requirements. This will allow an opportunity for program monitoring as outlined in Subsections 6.2.5, 7.5 and 7.6 to occur.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.1
Title: 6.1.1 HIV Case Manager
Section: 6.1.1
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2020-01-15
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Content:
An HIV CM shall meet one of the following qualifications:
Hold a master's degree from an accredited college or university in a human services field, including, but not limited to, social work, sociology, child development, maternal and child health, counseling, psychology, or nursing.
Hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited school of social work.
Hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in a human services field or related curriculum, including at least 15 semester hours in courses related to social work, counseling, or public health; and have six months of social work or counseling experience.
Hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university and have one year of experience in counseling or in a related human services field that provides experience in techniques of counseling, casework, group work, social work, public health, or human services.
Be licensed, if applicable, by the appropriate licensure board in North Carolina as a registered nurse, nurse practitioner, physician, physician assistant, or certified substance abuse counselor and have two years of experience working in human services.
In addition, the CM shall possess two years' case management experience. All CM's shall possess, or acquire through cross training, a clinical understanding of HIV, as evidenced by documentation in their personnel file.
A standard year of work experience is calculated at 2080 hours per calendar year. An accredited educational institution is one that is nationally recognized. Refer to a regional accreditation organization or the U.S. Department of Education Web site at http://www.ed.gov.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.2
Title: 6.1.2 Case Management Experience
Section: 6.1.2
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2020-01-15
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Content:
Case management experience must encompass the functions of intake, assessment, reassessment, care planning, case coordination, case conferencing, care plan implementation, referral, linkage and resource development, crisis intervention, monitoring and follow -up of services provided and discharge or termination.
The CM shall possess the following core competencies:
Able to perform the assessment;
Able to provide beneficiary-centered goals for meeting desired outcomes developed in the care plan;
Able to provide referral and linkage to beneficiaries serviced;
Able to provide effective and efficient monitoring of care and service rendered to beneficiaries; and
Able to provide documentation and attestation as to accuracy of the entry by personal signature.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.4
Title: 6.1.4 HIV Case Management Supervisor
Section: 6.1.4
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2020-01-15
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Content:
An HIV Case Management supervisor shall meet one of the following qualifications:
Hold a master's degree from an accredited college or university in a human services field, including, but not limited to, social work, sociology, child development, maternal and child health, counseling, psychology, or nursing; and one year of human services experience;
Hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited school of social work and have two years of human services experience;
Hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in a human services field or related curriculum, including at least 15 semester hours in courses related to social work or counseling and have two years of experience in human services or public health;
Hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university, and have either, three years of human services experience, or two years of human services experience plus one year of supervisory experience; or
Be licensed, if applicable, by the appropriate licensure board in North Carolina as a registered nurse, nurse practitioner, physician, physician assistant, or certified substance abuse counselor; and have either, three years of human services experience, or two years of human services experience plus one year of supervisory experience.
In addition, the CM's supervisor must possess three years' case management experience.

[getSection]
ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.7.2
Title: 6.1.7.2 Annual Training
Section: 6.1.7.2
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2020-01-15
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Content:
All HIV CMs and supervisors shall complete twelve (12) hours of continuing education related to HIV Case Management annually. It is the responsibility of providers to retain copies of certificates of completion.
Annual training topics must include, but are not limited to the following:
confidentiality;
cultural competency;
current trends in HIV disease management;
ethics;
refresher core components of case management; and
treatment of individuals who are HIV positive. Six hours of the twelve hour annual requirement must include clinically oriented training (clinical updates).
Suggested resources include, but are not limited to the following:
Partners in Information Access for the Public Health Workforce
Carolina Care Partnership
North Carolina AIDS Education Training Center

per_question.question: Will the Orthotics and Prosthetics policy (5B) pay for chiropractic treatment?
per_question.agent_answer:
No. Policy 5B covers **orthotics and prosthetics**, meaning devices and related supplies that meet the policy’s medical-necessity and provider-ordering criteria; it does not describe coverage for chiropractic treatment as a covered service under this policy. [Policy 5B § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment) [Policy 5B § 5.3.14](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

The policy’s covered items are orthotic devices, prosthetic devices, and related supplies when the underlying device is covered and the supply is necessary for the device’s function. [Policy 5B § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment) [Policy 5B § 5.3.14](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

Its not-covered section also speaks in terms of **devices and supplies**, not treatment services like chiropractic care. [Policy 5B § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

Policy 5B was marked current in the corpus, and I did not find a change notice making another document the authoritative replacement. [Policy 5B](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

If you want, I can also check whether **any other NC Medicaid policy** covers chiropractic treatment, separate from Policy 5B.

scores.explanation: The agent correctly answers 'No' and accurately explains that Policy 5B covers orthotic and prosthetic devices/supplies, not chiropractic treatment services. The core factual answer matches the reference. However, the agent cites specific section numbers (§3.2.1, §5.3.14, §4.2.1) which are supported by the Evidence block, so those citations are valid. The agent mentions these sections exist in the evidence, which checks out. Minor issue: the agent references '§5.3.14' and '§3.2.1' as if they directly address the chiropractic question, when they actually just describe covered devices/supplies - this is a slight embellishment but not a major hallucination. The answer is slightly less complete than the reference because it doesn't explicitly note that chiropractic services are governed by a different clinical coverage policy, though it does offer to check other policies. The citation format uses URLs rather than precise section-level text references, which is adequate but not ideal. Overall, a Medicaid policy expert would find this acceptable but not as thorough as the reference answer.

uncited_claims: Policy 5B covers **orthotics and prosthetics**, meaning devices and related supplies that meet the policy’s medical-necessity and provider-ordering criteria; it does not describe coverage for chiropractic treatment as a covered service under this policy.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:Attachment E
Title: Attachment E: Requesting Unlisted Orthotics and Prosthetics for Adults
Section: Attachment E
Policy: 5B
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
In compliance with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Home Health Final Rule, 42 CFR Part 440.70, please follow these guidelines when requesting medical necessity reviews for Orthotics and Prosthetics for adults not listed in Attachment B or the O&P fee schedule.
The general requirements and criteria set forth in clinical coverage policy 5B must be met. This includes, but is not limited to:
The device being requested must fit the definition of an orthotic or prosthetic;
The beneficiary must be enrolled in the NC Medicaid program and be eligible for the device;
The provider must be enrolled in the NC Medicaid program with an appropriate taxonomy;
The requested device must be safe, effective, economical and not intended for the convenience of the beneficiary, the beneficiary's caregiver, or the provider;
The device must be medical in nature, generally recognized as an accepted method of treatment, and must not be experimental or investigational;
The device must be ordered by a physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner;
The device must be medically necessary to maintain or improve a beneficiary's medical, physical or functional level, and appropriate for use in any non-institutional setting in which normal life activities take place;
A documented face-to-face encounter with the beneficiary and the ordering physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner related to the primary reason the beneficiary requires the device must have occurred no more than six months prior to the initiation of orthotics and prosthetics; and
The beneficiary's need for the device must be reviewed by the ordering physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner at least annually.
If the provider determines that the applicable requirements and criteria set forth in clinical coverage policy 5B have been met, then the provider may submit a completed Certificate of Medical Necessity/Prior Approval (CMN/PA) form and the usual supportive prior authorization documentation through NCTracks for a medical necessity review.
Providers may request non-covered, unlisted or restricted items using their identifiable HCPCS code. If no HCPCS code exists, providers may use the national miscellaneous code L8499 .
Items approved by this procedure may be manually priced. Please include the appropriate manual pricing documentation with the prior authorization request.
Providers should expect medical necessity reviews using this procedure to take longer than usual.
Claims for items approved using this procedure should also be submitted through NCTracks.
If denied, the provider and beneficiary will be notified, and normal beneficiary appeal rights will apply.
Providers will be notified if the device requested is covered by a different NC Medicaid policy area or waiver program.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:5.5
Title: 5.5 Orthotic and Prosthetic Limitations
Section: 5.5
Policy: 5B
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
Medicaid may place appropriate limits, based on medical necessity criteria, on Orthotics and Prosthetics. When the prescribing physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner, orders equipment or supplies beyond these limits, the provider shall seek prior authorization for these items through NCTracks.
A PA request for an override of a quantity limit, or lifetime expectancy must contain the usual PA documentation ( Subsections 5.2 and 5.3 ) along with the following additional information:
The item being requested for an override clearly marked on the CMN/PA form.
The type of override (quantity limit, or lifetime expectancy) clearly stated.
An explanation of the medical necessity for the override from the physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner, or therapist.
Override PA requests are reviewed for medical necessity as per usual PA review timelines. Override PA review outcomes are communicated to providers and beneficiaries in the same way as a typical PA request.
Refer to Attachment B for a listing of the established lifetime expectancies and quantity limitations for Orthotics and Prosthetics. To request a medical necessity review for an item not listed, refer to sections 1.0 , 2.2 and Attachment E for instructions.

Reason: Matched limitation.
Content:
Medicaid shall cover orthotics and prosthetics when the beneficiary meets all the following specific criteria:
they are ordered by a physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner;
they are medically necessary to maintain or improve a beneficiary's medical, physical or functional level, and appropriate for use in any noninstitutional setting in which normal life activities take place;
a documented face-to-face encounter with the beneficiary and the ordering physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner related to the primary reason the beneficiary requires orthotics and prosthetics has occurred no more than six (6) months prior to the initiation of orthotics and prosthetics; and
the beneficiary's need for orthotics and prosthetics is reviewed by the ordering physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner at least annually.
Medicaid covers orthotic and prosthetic services when they are medically necessary, and the beneficiary meets the specific coverage requirements for the device.
Orthotic devices are medically necessary when required to correct or prevent skeletal deformities, to support or align movable body parts, or to preserve or improve physical function.
Prosthetic devices are medically necessary as a replacement for all or part of the function of a permanently inoperative, absent, or malfunctioning body part. The beneficiary shall require the prosthesis for mobility, daily care, or rehabilitation purposes.
In addition, orthotic and prosthetic devices must be:
a reasonable and medically necessary part of the beneficiary's treatment plan;
consistent with the beneficiary's diagnosis and medical condition, particularly the functional limitations and symptoms exhibited by the beneficiary; and
of high quality, with replacement parts available and obtainable.
Medical doctors (MDs), doctors of osteopathic medicine (DOs), doctors of podiatric medicine (DPMs), physician assistants (PAs) and nurse practitioners (NPs) may provide certain orthotic and prosthetic devices when the devices are part of the beneficiary's current care and treatment. These professionals may provide devices as indicated in the Required Provider Certification column of Attachment B .
To be reimbursed for an orthotic or prosthetic device, the provider shall be enrolled as an appropriate board-certified provider for the specific device. Refer to Attachment B, which includes the Required Professional Certification for Orthotic and Prosthetic Devices.
For specific coverage requirements, refer to Subsection 5.3, Documenting Medical Necessity.
